The Walchand Legacy: From Foundation to Excellence
"Celebrating Decades of Academic Brilliance and Transformational Impact"
The legacy of WCE is built on a foundation of visionary educators who established rigorous academic standards and nurtured a culture of excellence. Over the decades, the college has evolved to embrace cutting-edge technology and innovative teaching methodologies, ensuring relevance in a rapidly changing world. From the pioneering efforts of its founding faculty to its global impact today, Walchand College of Engineering exemplifies the perfect blend of tradition and modernity.
1947
The foundation stone was laid by the Late Shri Dhondumama Sathe with a single program leading to a B.E. (Civil) degree.
1955
The college was renamed after Seth Walchand Hirachand as Walchand College of Engineering, followed by the commencement of B.E. (Mechanical) and B.E. (Electrical) along with three Diploma programs; Civil, Mechanical, and Electrical.
1965
In 1956, the inception of the Administrative Council marked a pivotal moment. Over the subsequent decade, this council, in collaboration with industry leaders, steered the operations, ushering in a distinctive paradigm within the realm of education. Distinguished figures from Walchand Industries, such as WIL, HCC, IHP, and others, offered commendable leadership, steering the development of the college through an administrative council.
1970
Walchand College excelled. Eminent figures, such as Dr. Radhakrishnan, Karmaveer Bhaurao Patil, and Yashwantrao Chavan graced Walchand College with their presence from 1947 to 1970.
1971
WCE stands out for its distinguished faculty, known for its exceptional proficiency, dedication, and commitment to providing high-quality education and guidance to students. Under their leadership, the college introduced Postgraduate programs and established a research center, marking a historic milestone as the first center within Shivaji University. This legacy of academic excellence has endured for four decades.
1977
The increase of government aid marked a pivotal moment for WCE, as it became the inaugural private engineering college to receive such support.
2003
Achieving a significant milestone, WCE proudly secured NBA Accreditation for five Undergraduate Programs, marking a pioneering achievement as the first institution within Shivaji University to attain this prestigious accreditation.
2005
WCE enthusiastically participated in the World Bank-sponsored TEQIP Scheme, marking the initiation of a series of funding in two decades and sponsorships from various agencies dedicated to the advancement of institute development and research at WCE. Notable sponsors include RGSTC, DST, MPCB, SGRF, and Sakal, among others.
2007
The college achieved autonomy status, marking a historic milestone as the first private engineering institution to attain such recognition.
2008
The college enhanced its facilities with a world-class library, spanning 50,000 sq. ft. Generously funded by the “Walchand Hirachand Memorial Trust,” it’s now named the “Ajit Gulabchand Central Library.” This expansive space houses a comprehensive collection of reading materials.
2021
WCE maintains a robust placement record, exemplified by the remarkable highest package of 1.3 Crore PA by Saurabh Pukale. It stands as the unique engineering college providing such exceptional placements. Notably, the college celebrated its Platinum Jubilee in the same year, symbolizing a rich legacy spanning 75 years. The industry’s trust in our skilled graduates is a testament to our unwavering commitment to both employability and academic excellence.
2023
The influence of WEC’s education is evident in the accomplishments of our students and alumni. WCE boasts a remarkable network of more than 25,000 alumni, creating a global influence. Among them, our esteemed alumna, Ms. Leena Nair, stands out as the CHANEL Global CEO based in London, England, ranking among the top 10 Indian-origin CEOs globally.

WCE at Glance
WCE at
Glance
Walchand College of Engineering Sangli (WCE), established in 1947, is one of India’s oldest, premier, and probably India’s first private engineering institution. With a rich history of over 75 years and a beautiful campus of over 90 acres, WCE Sangli is providing transformational learning experiences in various disciplines of engineering. It is partially aided by the Govt. of Maharashtra. It is one of the unique composite institutions having HIGHER EDUCATION courses and BOARD level courses on one campus.
WCE, approved by AICTE, offers autonomous UG, PG, and Ph.D. programs under Shivaji University, Kolhapur and it also offers affiliated non-autonomous Diploma programs of Maharashtra State Board of Technical Education (MSBTE). The institute is given autonomous status by University Grants Commission since 2007.
At present, around 2300 students are studying in various BTech programs, 250 students in MTech programs, and around 50 scholars are pursuing their Ph.D. programs at Shivaji University. More than 750 students are studying for Diplomas under MSBTE. WCE was first institute to get Major programs accredited by the National Board of Accreditation and WCE carries the distinction of getting an ‘A’ grade from the National Assessment and Accreditation Council  (NAAC), Bangalore.
The students of WCE get placed in reputed Multinational and Indian Companies such as Google, Microsoft, LinkedIn, Amazon, John Deere, Rakuten, P&G, Mahindra, TCS, Infosys, and many other companies. The alumni of WCE are placed in high positions in reputed companies and institutions around the world. With their contribution towards the development of the institution, WCE Sangli is strongly marching on the path of excellence in engineering education. WCE has achieved a series of milestones; the credit of which undoubtedly goes to dedicated faculty, encouraging management, and our brilliant students. WCE also has highly qualified and dedicated faculty members who are constantly involved in research and are associated with practicing engineering. Most of the faculty members hold Doctoral degrees and M Tech degrees from various IITs and IISc.
WCE aims at overall development of students with focus on Education, Employability and Employment. The Track Based Curriculum and Choice Based Credit System along with Value Added Professional and Life Skill Courses at WCE, enable students to choose appropriate path of their career. WCE also has a vibrant student club culture, having actively involved in various technical and co-curricular student activities. There are also department-wise student associations and professional student chapters, who organize programs to keep up with the current trends in technology and also for enhancing the student personality.
Some of the Key milestones of Walchand College of Engineering,
First Private Engineering College in Maharashtra, probably in India.
One of very few private engineering institutions in India, aided by the State.
One of the very few autonomous engineering colleges in Maharashtra from 2007.
One of very few institutions getting accredited by NBA since 2003
Successfully participated in the World Bank-funded Technical Quality Improvement Program (TEQIP) of   MHRD in all three phases from 2004 till 2020 with funding of more than 30 Cr.
WCE mentored Jabalpur College of Engineering, Jabalpur.
No wonder WCE Sangli is the most preferred destination for engineering education today!

Chairman
Chairman
Shri. Ajit Gulabchand
Chairman, Administrative Council of WCE Sangli
Shri. Ajit Gulabchand is Chairman of the Administrative Council of WCE Sangli. He has provided vision, direction, and able leadership to the development of Walchand College of Engineering since 1997.
He is Chairman of the Hindustan Construction Company (HCC) – one of India’s leading construction companies, founded by industrialist Seth Walchand Hirachand in 1926. A catalytic factor in the infrastructure growth of India, HCC has accomplished various pioneering achievements in the engineering and construction industry under his leadership.
A graduate of Mumbai University, he began his career as the Chief Executive of Indian Hume Pipe Co. Ltd. and subsequently moved on to Ravalgaon Sugar Farm Ltd. as Managing Director, steering the company towards fast-track growth.
At the helm of affairs in HCC since 1983, Mr. Gulabchand has been credited with a slew of path-breaking strategic management initiatives. Today, HCC is an acknowledged leader in the engineering and construction sector in India. A modern and vibrant construction company, it has kept pace with modern technology, is committed to quality and boasts of a knowledge asset of more than 3000 people.
HCC is a business group of global scale developing and building responsible infrastructure through next practices. With an engineering heritage of nearly 100 years, HCC has executed a majority of India’s landmark infrastructure projects, having constructed 26% of India’s Hydro Power generation and 60% of India’s Nuclear Power generation capacities, over 4,036 lane km of Expressways and Highways, more than 360 km of complex Tunnelling and 395 Bridges. Today, HCC Ltd. serves the infrastructure sectors of Transportation, Power and Water.
Mr. Gulabchand is the visionary behind free India’s largest hill station, Lavasa, near Pune. Lavasa is spread across a picturesque landscape of 12,500 acres, set amidst 7 hills and 60 kms of lakefront.
Recognizing the importance of knowledge assets for building world class infrastructure, Mr. Gulabchand has the taken lead in ideating new concepts by investing in technical education and skills enhancement for HCC’s manpower and other training and technical institutions in the country such as NICMAR and the Walchand College of Engineering.
Corporate social responsibility remains intrinsic to Mr. Gulabchand’s vision for the group encompassing HIV, education, water, and disaster management initiatives. With a view to create a greater AIDS awareness in the industry, he has been instrumental in launching a work place intervention (WPI) program, covering more than 20,000 construction workers across HCC’s project locations.
Acknowledged for his visionary leadership in the industry, Mr. Gulabchand plays an important role in key industry bodies in India. He is a member of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) National Council and the Chairman of CII’s National Committee on Construction and Projects. He has also served as a founding permanent member of the board of governors of the construction industry development council of India (CIDC). He initiated the formation of the Construction Federation of India (CFI) with other construction companies and is the founder and president since its inception in 2001.
Mr. Gulabchand is the Governor and steering board member of the Engineering and Construction community at the World Economic Forum, Geneva, and a member of the CII-World Economic Forum Infrastructure Task Force. He is also a founder member of the Geneva-based Disaster Resource Network (DRN) in collaboration with the World Economic Forum, the United Nations, and International Red Cross. As Chairman of DRN India, he has been involved in disaster management during a number of natural disasters in India and abroad. He has also recently endowed a new ‘Ajit Gulabchand Chair’ on Indian Business Studies being set up at Oxford University and is a member of the Oxford International Advisory Board for Executive Education. He is also a signatory member of the United Nations Global Compact’s CEO Water Mandate.
Mr. Gulabchand’s other associations with industry bodies include,
Chairman for the Projects Exports Promotion Council (PEPC).
Past President and Permanent Member of the Governing Council of the Builders Association of India (BAI).
Chairman of the Board of Governors and Member of the Board of Trustees at the National Institute of Construction Management and Research (NICMAR), Pune.
Chancellor of NICMAR University of Construction Studies
Chairman of the Administrative Council of Walchand College of Engineering, Sangli.
Mr Gulabchand is a keen follower of sports and an ardent philanthropist.

MTE Society
Maharshtra Technical Education Society (MTE Society)
Late Shri. Dhondumama Sathe
Maharshtra Technical Education Society (MTES) is founded in 1945 by Late Shri. Dhondumama Sathe along with Hon’ble Shri. Datto Waman Potdar, Shri. Pudmjee, Shri. C.G. Agashe, Shri. M. V. Bhide, Shri. M. V. Shah, Shri. R. G. Sule and others, at Pune, Maharashtra.
Dhondo Krishna Sathe, popularly known as Dhondumama Sathe  , Long before the term became popular, he was one of the first serial entrepreneur from Pune.  Dhondumama created a name for himself as a building contractor. Some of the notable landmarks that he constructed include the SP College at Pune, The Pune Railway Station Building, Ruia College, Mumbai, New English School Pune, Aryan Education Society at Girgaon, Mumbai. The artistic canopy of Lokmanya Tiak’s status at Mahatma Phule Mandai in Pune was built by him. Dhondumama took sincere efforts to establish a new private bank – Bank of Maharashtra that was set up in 1935.
Dhondumama was very passionate about industry and commerce and was convinced of its positive role in the development of the country. Trained people were the bedrock for any meaningful progress. Those days there was a solitary engineering college in Pune offering degree in engineering. This catered to the erstwhile Bombay state that also included parts of Gujarat and North Karnataka. Dhondumama was consumed by a new passion of setting up an engineering college to provide skilled experts who would contribute in the industrial development. He worked hard to achieve the dream and set up the Maharashtra Technical Education Society. The plan was to start the college in Pune. However at the request of then Chief Minister B G Kher it was decided to establish it elsewhere since Pune already had an engineering college. The Rajesaheb of Sangli and the Walchand Group supported his efforts and the college was established in Sangli. The New Engineering College was established in 1947. The college was renamed Walchand College of Engineering in 1955 after Walchand Trust rescued and rehabilitated this college from trouble.  The then Vice President Dr S Radhakrishnan graced this function the chief guest.
He supported a large number of students to complete their education by providing assistance in cash or kind. Dhondumama’s wide social circle was also part of his endevaours. N C Kelkar, Datto Waman Potdar, F D Pudumjee, Chandrashekhar Agashe, N G Pawar, N V Gadgil, A R Bhat and other prominent citizens were his associates in many of the ventures.

Seth Walchand Hirachand Doshi
Seth Walchand Hirachand Doshi (1882-1953) was a visionary Indian industrialist and a pivotal figure in India’s industrial development during the pre-independence era. He is often hailed as the “Father of Transportation in India” due to his groundbreaking ventures in key industries, laying the groundwork for a self-reliant India.
Seth Walchand Hirachand Doshi’s career was characterized by an audacious vision and relentless drive to establish indigenous industries in pre-independence India. He dared to venture into sectors dominated by British enterprises, laying the foundation for a self-reliant India.
Glance at Seth Walchand’s Contribution to India’s Growth
Pioneer in diverse sectors: Late Seth Walchand established businesses across a spectrum of industries, including civil engineering, aircraft manufacturing, maritime shipping, shipbuilding, automobile manufacturing, organized farming, sugar factories, and more.
Founded
India’s first modern shipyard, aircraft factory, and car factory
: He founded the Hindustan Aircraft Company (later
Hindustan Aeronautics Limited – HAL
) in 1940, Scindia Shipyard (later
Hindustan Shipyard Limited
) in Visakhapatnam in 1940, and
Premier Automobiles
Limited (PAL) near Mumbai in 1945. These companies played a crucial role in establishing India’s industrial base in these critical sectors.
Driving force behind Scindia Steam Navigation Company: He founded the
Scindia Steam Navigation Company
in 1919, challenging British dominance in the Indian shipping industry. The maiden voyage of the company’s ship, “SS Loyalty,” on April 5, 1919, from Mumbai to London, is now celebrated as
National Maritime Day in India
.
Significant contributions to construction: His early success in the construction business, initially as a railway contractor, led to the establishment of Hindustan Construction Company in 1926, which remains a leading engineering and construction company in India today.
Hindustan Construction Company
is credited with executing major projects like the tunnels through the Bhor Ghats for a railway route from Mumbai to Pune and laying water pipes from Tansa Lake to Mumbai.
Agricultural Revolution and Industrial Townships: Walchand’s vision extended to agriculture, he transformed barren land into sugarcane fields and established
Walchandnagar Industries
Limited in 1934 and the establishment of the industrial township of Walchandnagar. Walchandnagar Industries Limited (WIL) in 1934, which diversified into sugar, heavy engineering, and defense manufacturing, supplying critical equipment for India’s programs.
Associated industries and organizations: Walchand also ventured into insurance and was a founder member and leader of various industry associations.
Many of Walchand’s ventures faced challenges like foreign competition and nationalization. However, his entrepreneurial spirit, patriotism, and belief in India’s potential left an indelible mark.
Walchand Hirachand’s contributions are still recognized:
He is known as the “Father of Transportation in India”.
The Indian government issued a postage stamp in his honor in 2004.
A road in Mumbai is named after him.
Seth Walchand Hirachand’s career exemplifies a life dedicated to industrialization and nation-building.
Walchand Hirachand Memorial Trust (WHMT) was established to support charitable and educational activities. It was led by his brothers Seth Lalchand Hirachand and Seth Gulabchand Hirachand. WHMT, at the request of late Dhondomama Sathe on behalf of MTE Society and both State as well as Central Governments, came forward to support WCE in 1955 under rehabilitation and development of then NEW ENGINEERING COLLEGE, which was renamed WALCHAND COLLEGE OF ENGINERING.

Director
Dr. Surendra Singh Rathod
Director
Dr. Surendra Singh Rathod currently serves as the Director of Walchand College of Engineering, Sangli. Prior to this, he held the position of Principal at Fr. Conceicao Rodrigues College of Engineering, Bandra, Mumbai, for three years. His distinguished career also includes 24 years of service at Sardar Patel Institute of Technology (S.P.I.T.), Mumbai, where he contributed in multiple leadership roles such as Professor, Head of the Department (Electronics Engineering), and Dean (Academics). A seasoned academician, researcher, and visionary leader in technical education, Dr. Rathod brings over two decades of rich experience in teaching, research, and academic administration. He has played a pivotal role in enhancing engineering education and institutional growth. Dr. Rathod earned his Ph.D. in Engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Roorkee, maintaining an exceptional academic track record. His research expertise encompasses cutting-edge domains like VLSI Design, ASIC Verification, Artificial Intelligence, and Engineering Education. Under his supervision, seven scholars have successfully completed their Ph.D., and his extensive publications in reputed national and international journals reflect his scholarly depth. He is also actively involved with various professional bodies, Academic Councils, Boards of Studies, and Governing Councils across institutions. He has been always at the forefront of shaping a student-centric learning ecosystem. A strong proponent of student-centered education, Dr. Rathod envisions developing young engineers as both competent technocrats and socially responsible citizens. His commitment to integrating Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS), fostering innovation, strengthening industry-academia partnerships, and promoting holistic education continues to inspire students and faculty. Guided by his principles of excellence, ethics, and nation-building, Dr. S. S. Rathod stands as a beacon in the advancement of engineering education.

Deputy Director
Deputy Director
Prof. Dr. Udaykumar Anna Dabade
Deputy Director
Prof. Dr. Udaykumar Anna Dabade is a visionary leader and a distinguished academician who has been instrumental in shaping the destiny of Walchand College of Engineering, Sangli. As the Officiating I/C Director of the institution since March 2023, he has brought his wealth of experience and expertise to the table, providing strategic leadership and guidance to the college. With a strong academic background in Mechanical Engineering, having completed his B.E. from WCE in 1994 and M. Tech. and Ph.D. from IIT Bombay, Prof. Dabade has specialized in areas such as Manufacturing, Production, Micromachining, Precision Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Difficult to cut materials, Advanced Manufacturing Technology and Materials Science etc. His research interests have led to the publication of over 155 research papers, guiding 5 Ph.D. research scholars, 75+ M.E./ M.Tech dissertation and securing funding of ₹70+ lakhs from DST, AICTE, and UGC for research and travel grants. A recipient of the DST Young Scientist Award, Prof. Dabade has also demonstrated his leadership acumen by serving as State Project Administrator (SPA) for the TEQIP project in Rajasthan, appointed by the Ministry of Education (GoI). With a strong international exposure, having traveled to 11 countries for conferences and research paper publications, Prof. Dabade has also delivered expert lectures at various workshops and conferences. As a professional, he is a member of prestigious organizations such as ISTE, ITPE, IIIE, IACSIT, IET, and ASME. With his exceptional leadership qualities, academic excellence, and research expertise, Prof. Dr. Udaykumar Anna Dabade is poised to take Walchand College of Engineering, Sangli, to greater heights.

Regular Admissions for Indian Students
Walchand College of Engineering admits students to its undergraduate B. Tech programs at in First Year Four Year Course through the Centralised Admission Process (CAP) conducted by the State Common Entrance Test Cell, Maharashtra.
Aided and Unaided Programs
Walchand College of Engineering offers both aided and unaided B. Tech Programs. Aided courses are basically financed by Government of Maharashtra. Since institute is partially aided institute (90% of salary of aided courses), teacher and staff salary to large extent is supported from government aid (fund), For unaided courses, salary component of staff and faculty, as well other expenses are primarily dependent on student fees.
From the students’ perspective, there is no difference between aided and unaided courses in terms of syllabus, teaching-learning processes, exam patterns, infrastructure, state-of-the-art laboratory facilities, access to government student related schemes, placement opportunities etc.
Base for Admission tests
Aided Courses –  Admissions to aided courses are based solely on the CET examination.
Unaided Courses –  Admissions to unaided courses are through the CAP process, with 15% seats reserved for candidates who have qualified for JEE (Main) and the remaining 85% seats filled through CET.

Eligibility Criteria for HSC/ XIIth in addition to test as above -
To be eligible for admission to Walchand College of Engineering, candidates must satisfy the following conditions:
Passed the HSC (Std. XII) examination of Maharashtra State Board of Secondary and Higher Secondary Education or its equivalent examination with subjects English, Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics.
Obtained a minimum of 50% marks (45% for backward class candidates from Maharashtra) in the subjects Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics added together.
For Domicile and other conditions , one should refer CAP cell guidelines.
Centralised Admission Process (CAP)
The Centralised Admission  Process (CAP) is conducted by the State Common Entrance Test Cell, Maharashtra. The admission process involves the following steps:
Registration_: Candidates must register online for CAP on the official website.
Document Verification_: Candidates must verify their documents at designated Facilitation Centres (FCs).
Option Form Filling_: Candidates must fill in their preferred college and course options in multiple rounds ( CAP1, CAP2, CAP3 etc)
Seat Allocation_: Seats are allocated to candidates based on their merit and preferences.
Reporting to College_: Candidates must report to the allocated college to confirm their admission once student confirms allotment through CAP
Fees
Fees for aided courses are as decided by State Government competent authority (DTE)
Fees for unaided courses are as decided by Fees Regulatory Authority of state of Maharashtra.
Scholarships
The various scholarship schemes are applicable to students getting admitted in the college. SC/ST/NT student gets full wavier of fees while OBC /EBC /SBC /SEBC  students gets 50% wavier in fees.

Institute level Admissions at FY level
For aided courses , there are no institute level seats
For unaided courses , institute level seats are surrendered to CAP hence no institute level seats/ management quota
5 seats are nominated by Walchand Hirachand Memorial Trust and 2 seats are nominated by D D Daruwala Trust , as per agreement between them with State in 1955 and directions of State accordingly
Vacancies against CAP
Institute advertises for admission against CAP vacancies and invites applications and fills all seats as per directions of CET cell inter se merit in respective category of seats
Detailed notification can be seen here………. click below link (
https://cetcell.mahacet.org/
)
Tuition Fee Waiver Scheme (TFWS)Seats
There shall be supernumerary ( in addition to above intake capacity up to maximum 5 percent of sanctioned intake) seats under Tuition Fee Wavier scheme  as per directions of AICTE/ GoI/ GoM. These seats are part of CAP process and state CET Cell/DTE will notify these in accordance with regulations during admission process
Eligibility
(i) Only Maharashtra State Candidature candidates are eligible for these seats
(ii) Eligible Maharashtra State Candidates having their parent’s annual income less than Rs. 8 Lakh (Rupees Eight Lakh only) from all sources shall only be eligible for these seats. The candidate shall submit Income certificate issued by Appropriate Authority.
(iii) These seats are allotted by the Competent Authority as per inter-se merit. For this purpose, the Competent Authority shall invite applications, prepare a separate merit list for this category by following the same criteria as for Maharashtra State Candidature Candidates. In the event of non-availability of students in this category the same shall not be given to any other category of applicants.

within fifty(50) kilometer radial distance from the Institute.
The candidate shall have Minimum of one Year Full time or Regular working Experience in the prescribed format available at CET website in Registered Industry or Organization (Central or State) or Private or Public Limited Company or Micro Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME’s).
Additional notes
The mode of Conduct of Classes shall be as applicable for Regular Programs as defined in the AICTE Public Notice Vide. No. AICTE/AB/Academic/2020-21, dated 13th August, 2020(In Regular Face to Face Mode).
Minimum admission required to run the course shall be 1/3 of the approved intake in each course.
One seat in every Institute shall be Reserved for Candidates working in the Central Government Organizations or Industries or Companies or Autonomous Organizations purely on MERIT Basis. In absence of any such Candidate, the vacant seat shall be transferred to General Category.
Working Professionals provisionally admitted in a course of the institute where total admissions in a course are less than 1/3 rd of approved intake of the course after pre cut-off date for admissions shall be transferred strictly on merit basis in the nearby institute within 50 kilo meter radial distance from the working industry or organization in the same course or different course in case vacancy exists in nearby institutes on the request of the candidate.
Provisional Admission of the candidate shall be cancelled automatically if the candidate is not able to secure the admission on merit against vacancy in other institutes.
This process of transfer shall be carried out between Pre cut-off date and cut-off date for admissions to working professionals.
Institute having admissions below 1/3 rd admissions after Pre cut-off date has to refund full fees to the candidate in case of cancellation/transfer of admission immediately within two days of cancellation or transfer of admission
Any other eligibility criteria or requirements declared from time to time by the appropriate authority and AICTE as defined under the Act.
Centralised Admission  Process (CAP)
The Centralised Admission  Process (CAP) is conducted by the State Common Entrance Test Cell, Maharashtra. The admission process involves the following steps:
Registration_: Candidates must register online for CAP on the official website.
Document Verification_: Candidates must verify their documents at designated Facilitation Centres (FCs).
Option Form Filling_: Candidates must fill in their preferred college and course options in multiple rounds ( CAP1, CAP2, CAP3 etc)
Seat Allocation_: Seats are allocated to candidates based on their merit and preferences.
Reporting to College_: Candidates must report to the allocated college to confirm their admission once student confirms allotment through CAP

Policy and guidelines for working professionals’ courses in Walchand College of Engineering for engagement of classes , examination etc
This will be a full-time regular program, but timing will be adjusted as per the convenience of working professionals
The program will follow the same structure as the usual full-time program, including the curriculum and credit requirements. Students will adhere to the same academic pattern and will take the same examinations as their full-time counterparts.
The lecture engagement will differ from the regular programs
This will be a separate division as called ‘W’
Every Monday to Friday on all working days, a minimum 2 hours of lecture engagement will happen on the premises or through online mode via VC or equivalent platforms
The online platform will be used only for the delivery of lectures and attendance shall be recorded.
Laboratory work and tutorials will be conducted on Saturday and/ or Sunday as per the department’s priority
It will be ensured that in case Saturday is working for students in their employment at least half a day concession shall be granted
The laboratory or tutorial engagement to the tune of 8 to 14 hours shall be engaged on weekends in offline mode only.
As with other students and ordinances applicable to them.  100% performance in lab sessions/tutorials is mandatory and requisite attendance in theory lectures in online/offline mode is also mandatory
The teachers teaching this load will be remunerated   as per college policy considering this as an additional load and  supporting staff also shall be given additional remuneration as per the policy
For Any seminar/project/mini project /
slash
research project a preference shall be given to the project from the employer organization. During project mentoring/guidance, the student is expected to report in person on campus at least once a week fortnight along with a progress report and the rest of the time online.
In case of the provision of internship, their experience in the employer organization shall be considered equivalent
Any initiative towards employability shall be extended to these students also in case students wish to enroll for it however students will not be offered any employment assistant/opportunity as they are working professionals, and their employer has supported joining this course so it is expected that the benefit of additional knowledge of post-graduation should be first utilized in the current organization
The engagement on public holidays shall be compensated by taking additional load with the mutual consent of students on some alternative days.
No separate arrangements shall be made for terminal examinations. Students will appear along with regular full-time students. Mid-Sem exam and other assessments may be re-aligned to weekends or other alternative media.

Overview
Overview: Department of Civil Engineering
The Department of Civil Engineering was the first inchoative discipline at Walchand College of Engineering, Sangli, and the oldest in the Southern Maharashtra region. Starting its journey in 1947, the department has contributed to producing several eminent engineers who are in key positions of the Government organisations, public sector and infrastructure companies, and have brought in significant contributions in the planning and execution of Civil Engineering projects in various regions of India.
The Department offers a four-year programme leading to the Bachelor’s Degree in Civil Engineering (B. Tech.) and a two-year programme leading to a Master’s degree (M. Tech.) in Civil Engineering with specialisation in Environmental Engineering and Construction Management.
The Department is known for its reputed faculty, having expertise in diverse fields. The faculty of the department continues to strive loftier by exploring new frontiers of civil engineering, imparting the latest technical knowledge to the students, and conducting high-quality research. The faculty has contributed more than a hundred research papers in various Journals and Conferences. The faculty also renders technical advice on live engineering problems in the field of Geotechnical, Structural, Environmental, Hydraulics, Transportation and Water Resources   Engineering, etc., to various Government and Private Sector companies throughout the state. It has built up a wide research potential in Structural and Environmental Engineering. The department also has other well-equipped engineering laboratories in the field of concrete and material testing, Geotechnical, Hydraulics, Transportation, Surveying, and Construction. Apart from the Central computing facility, the department has its own computing facility with more than 60 nodes and continuous internet access. The research projects of the department are funded by various agencies such as the Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD), All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), Department of Science and Technology (DST), Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB), Fund for Improvement of S&T infrastructure (FIST), MODROB, TEQIP, etc.
The department has a rich legacy of accomplishments, including:
The department has a rich legacy of accomplishments, including:
Consistent top rankings in national and international competitive exams like GATE, MPSC, IES, IAS.
Alumni excelling as technology leaders, innovators, and researchers across the globe.
Along with the academics and Teaching-Learning process, the department has a strong Mentor-Mentee System by virtue of which students and faculty will interact to ensure a wholesome development of students as an Engineer and a responsible citizen.
Objectives
The Department of Civil Engineering aims to achieve the following objectives:
To achieve a high level of technical expertise to understand, identify, formulate, design, and implement a real-life Civil Engineering problem.
To inculcate leadership and ethical qualities in implementing the projects.
To produce technically competent and ethically sound engineering graduates.
To satisfy the requirements of society through active participation in infrastructural development.
To prepare the students for competitive examinations, research, and higher education.
To induce qualities of lifelong learning, working in teams with effective communication skills and interaction with society.
Vision
To be a Civil Engineering programme of the first choice by the aspiring students and prospective employers by implementing world-class education practices.
Mission
To meet the Vision, all stakeholders of this programme are committed to Outcome-Based Education Philosophy by
Adopting vibrant academic curricula and implementing innovative teaching-learning processes.
Providing opportunities to the students for the development of professional skills.
Nurturing critical thinking and creativity in students.
Inculcating in students a life-long learning attitude and sensitivity towards society & environment.
Strength
The Department of Civil Engineering stands out for its key strengths, which include:
Experienced and Dedicated Faculty
Robust Curriculum in line with NEP2020
Well-equipped and State-of-Art Infrastructure
Well-equipped laboratories
Strong Industry Connections
High Placement Record
Holistic Development Opportunities
Global Alumni Network
Research Projects on live problems
Continuous Improvement
These strengths collectively position the department as a key stakeholder in civil engineering education, research and innovation.
Areas of Expertise
The Department of Civil Engineering excels in the following areas of expertise:
Building Construction Technology and Materials
Construction Management
Environmental Engineering
Geology & Geotechnical Engineering
Hydraulics
Remote Sensing and GIS
Soil Mechanics
Structures
Surveying
Transportation Engineering
Water Resources
These areas of expertise enable the department to provide students with advanced knowledge and practical skills, preparing them for leadership roles in the ever-evolving technology landscape.
Salient Department Features
The Department of Civil Engineering at Walchand College of Engineering stands out for its unique features and strengths, including:
Academic Excellence:
NEP-2020 aligned curriculum focusing on foundational and advanced topics, along with the practical, industrial requirements.
Highly qualified faculty with expertise in salient areas of civil engineering and related upgrading technologies. Nearly 80% of faculty members have a Ph.D. and Ph. D. registered.
State-of-the-Art Infrastructure:
Modern technology incorporates high-end performance labs with high-performance systems and equipment.
Access to advanced tools, software, and a dedicated Departmental Computing facility.
Research and Innovation:
Active research in emerging fields like building materials, sustainable development, and real-time environmental problems.
Regular attendance and publications in reputed journals and conference participations with Scopus and SCI indexing.
Strong Industry Interface:
Collaborations, MoUs with leading Construction and Civil Engineering related companies in the Public and Private sector for internships, placements, and projects.
Expert guest lectures, workshops, and certification trainings.
Skill Development Opportunities:
Emphasis on hands-on learning through in-house training, seminars, and projects.
Active technical clubs, local chapters of reputed associations, and student organisations fostering innovation.
Global Competence:
Alumni are placed in top organisations and are pursuing higher education globally.
Exposure to international competitions and exchange programs.
Student-Centric Environment:
Strong mentor-mentee system by faculty for academic and professional growth.
Focus on holistic development through extracurricular and co-curricular activities.
Placement Excellence:
High placement rates with opportunities in top companies in the public and private sectors.
Dedicated training for technical interviews, on-field experiences, and soft skills.
Continuous Improvement:
Regular updates to the curriculum and teaching methodologies.
Feedback-driven enhancements for a superior learning experience.
These features collectively position the department as a leader in producing highly skilled, innovative, and socially responsible engineers.
Leadership
Dr. Amol K. Mali
(Head of the Department of Civil Engineering)
Dr. Amol K. Mali is the Head of the Department of Civil Engineering at Walchand College of Engineering, Sangli. He joined the institution in 2009, and since then, he has made a significant contribution to the Civil Engineering Department and Walchand College of Engineering as a whole through his expertise, research, and education. Dr. Mali holds a Ph.D. in Civil Engineering from IIT, Bombay, Mumbai. He has earned his M. Tech. and B.E. degrees in Civil Engineering from IIT, Roorkee, and KIT’s College of Engineering, Kolhapur, respectively.
Prior to academic experience, he has a great experience of working in reputed construction sector companies in Bridge Design and Concrete Quality Control.
His research interests include Construction Management, Concrete Technology, and Transportation Engineering. Dr. Mali has published numerous papers in national and international journals and conferences. He has also been involved in several sponsored projects. He has served in various responsibilities and capacities at the department and institute levels during his tenure.
With his long industrial and academic experience, along with visionary leadership skills,
Dr. Amol Mali is leading the Department of Civil Engineering at Walchand College of Engineering, Sangli

Overview
Overview: Department of Applied Mechanics
The Department of Applied Mechanics at Walchand College of Engineering (WCE), Sangli, is a premier center for advanced education and research in structural engineering. Specializing in M.Tech (Civil-Structural Engineering) and Ph.D. programs, the department combines academic rigor with real-world applications through a curriculum aligned with industry and global standards.
Renowned for its research in structural, earthquake, bridge, and railway engineering, as well as FEA, sustainable infrastructure, and structural health monitoring, the department maintains strong industry ties through consultancy, structural audits, and collaborative projects.
Equipped with state-of-the-art labs and advanced software tools, it fosters innovation, hands-on learning, and interdisciplinary problem-solving. Alumni hold key positions in industry, academia, and government, reflecting the department’s commitment to excellence, professional development, and leadership in infrastructure engineering.
Placement Data
Student List
Faculty List
Objectives
The Department of Applied mechanics aims to achieve the following objectives:
To achieve high level of technical expertise to understand, identify, formulate, design and implement a real-life structural engineering problem.
To satisfy the requirement of society through active participation in infrastructural development with leadership and ethical principles.
To inculcate individual critical thinking in analysing the complex problems in structural engineering field.
To build capacity in upcoming areas of research in structural engineering.
To induce qualities of effective communication skills, working in teams and lifelong learning.
Policy
The Department of Applied Mechanics is dedicated to excellence in education, research, industry collaboration, and professional ethics. It aims to develop skilled engineers and innovators who contribute to sustainable infrastructure and societal advancement.
Vision
To be a Structural Engineering Program of the first choice by the aspiring students and prospective employers by implementing world class educational and research practices.
Mission
To implement Outcome Based Education Philosophy effectively by.
Adopting dynamic academic curricula, implementing innovative teaching learning processes and research practices.
Providing opportunities to the students for the development of professional skills.
Nurturing critical thinking and creativity in the students.
Inculcating in the student’s life-long learning attitude with sensitivity towards society and environment.
Strengths
The Department of Applied Mechanics stands out for its key strengths, which include:
Highly experienced faculty
Well-structured and industry-relevant curriculum
Advanced laboratories and software tools
Research-driven approach
Strong industry and government collaborations
Structural testing and consultancy services
Expertise in structural audits for public and private sector projects
High success rate in competitive examinations (UPSC, MPSC, etc.)
Comprehensive professional development opportunities
Accomplished alumni network
Commitment to continuous quality improvement
These strengths collectively position the department as a leader in applied mechanics, structural engineering, infrastructure research, and consultancy.
Areas of Expertise
The Department of Applied Mechanics excels in the following areas of expertise:
Earthquake Engineering
Railway Engineering
Bridge Design and Analysis
Finite Element Analysis (FEA)
Computational Mechanics
Advanced Concrete Technology
Smart Materials and Structures
Structural Fire Engineering
Structural Health Monitoring
Seismic Retrofitting and Rehabilitation of Structures
Structural Audits and Condition Assessments
Soil-Structure Interaction
Sustainable Infrastructure Development
Composite Materials
These areas of expertise enable the department to prepare students for leadership roles in structural, and infrastructure engineering sectors.
Salient Department Features
The Department of Applied Mechanics at Walchand College of Engineering stands out for its unique features and strengths, including:
Academic Excellence:
Rigorous curriculum aligned with national and international standards.
Faculty members with extensive industry and research experience.
Nearly 85% of faculty registered for or holding PhDs.
State-of-the-Art Infrastructure:
Advanced laboratories for structural testing, material testing, and CAD/FEA.
Access to high-end software tools like COMSOL, MIDAS Civil etc.
Research and Innovation:
Active research in structural dynamics, bridge engineering, railway infrastructure, earthquake-resistant design, and sustainability.
Regular publications in Scopus, SCI-indexed journals, and participation in conferences.
Research outputs in the form of IPR and Patents.
Industry and Government Interface:
Collaborations with leading companies, public works departments, Indian Railways, and government agencies for testing, structural audits, and consultancy projects.
Expert-led guest lectures, workshops, and technical certifications.
Skill Development Opportunities:
Hands-on learning through design projects, consultancy assignments, field visits, and technical competitions.
Active participation in professional societies like ISTE, IEI, ISET, ISWE, IGS, IIBE, ICI, and ISSE.
Global Competence:
Alumni contributing to major infrastructure projects globally and pursuing higher education at premier institutes.
Participation in international conferences and technical collaborations.
Student-Centric Environment:
Mentorship by faculty for academic, personal, and professional growth.
Opportunities for leadership through workshops, and community service.
Placement and Professional Success:
Strong placement records in leading MNCs, design consultancies, testing and audit firms, and government organizations.
Consultancy Excellence:
The department provides professional testing, structural audit, proof-checking, and third-party inspection services for public and private sector building infrastructure and civil engineering projects.
In the year 2024–25, the department successfully executed consultancy work exceeding ₹1.25 crore.
Significant contribution to ensuring structural safety, quality assurance, and code compliance in major infrastructure works.
Expert contribution as a structural engineer for arbitration and legal/ court matters.
Continuous Improvement:
Regular curriculum review and pedagogical innovations.
Feedback-driven updates to ensure alignment with industry advancements and future trends.
These features highlight the department as a centre of excellence, producing highly skilled, innovative, and socially responsible engineers and consultants.
Leadership
Dr. Sachin Balasaheb Kadam
(Head of the  Department of Applied Mechanics)
Dr. Sachin Balasaheb Kadam is a distinguished academician and researcher in field of Civil-Structural Engineering. Currently serving as Professor and Head of the Department of Applied Mechanics at Walchand College of Engineering, Sangli, he has extensive experience in teaching, research, and administration. His expertise exhibit in domain of structural analysis, seismic design, structural health monitoring, finite element analysis, and structural fire engineering.
Dr. Kadam earned his Ph.D. in Structural Dynamics from Department of Earthquake Engineering, IIT Roorkee in 2014, following his M.E. in Civil (Structural) Engineering from Shivaji University, Kolhapur, in 2002 and B.E. in Civil Engineering from the same university in 1997. His professional career includes roles as a Structural Engineer at Reliance Industries Ltd. and a Junior Engineer at L&T ECC Ltd., before transitioning into academia in year 2004. He taught all major courses on analysis and design of structures in Civil Engineering. He supervised and guided 72 M.Tech. Dissertations in Structural Engineering and also guiding 4 students for their doctorate degree out of which 1 student has awarded Ph.D. degree. He has h index of 8 (i-10 index of 7, total citations exceeding 343 +, Source: Google Scholar, June 2025.) and four patents granted in India and Australia. He has worked as reviewer for reputed international journals. He has also authored a book and lead major research projects, including a ₹1.03 crore DST-FIST ongoing grant for pseudo dynamic test setup and research grant from MORTH and NTU Singapore.
In addition to his research contributions, Dr. Kadam has played crucial administrative roles, serving as the Registrar of Walchand College of Engineering from 2020 to 2023, Chief Rector of institute hostel from 2017 to 2020, and a Board of Studies (BOS) member in civil engineering at Shivaji University since 2023. He is an active member of professional organizations such as ISET, ISTE, ISWE, and IGS, and holds a membership with the Institution of Engineers (India) and American Concrete Institute. His achievements have been recognized with prestigious award of Young Scientist by the Uttarakhand State Science & Technology Congress in 2011 and Best Paper Award (Taylor and Francis’s Publication) in 2023 organised by Chandigarh University, Punjab.

M.Tech Design (15 intake)
programs for working professionals are offered. The department is recognized as a
Research Centre for Ph.D.
under
Shivaji University
, as well as through
AICTE QIP and ADF schemes
.
The
B.Tech program
is accredited by
NBA
till
June 2027
, marking its
fifth accreditation cycle
, while the postgraduate programs have also been accredited
three times
. With
around 70% of faculty holding Ph.D.s
, the department engages in research across
Design, Manufacturing, Thermal, Industrial Engineering
, and
interdisciplinary domains
.
As an
autonomous institute
, the curriculum is regularly updated per
NEP 2020
guidelines to incorporate industry trends, emerging technologies, and outcome-based learning. A dedicated
Board of Studies (BoS)
, comprising faculty, industry experts, alumni, and students, oversees curriculum design.
Students can pursue
B.Tech (Honours)
in
Turbomachinery
and
Mathematical Applications
, or a
Minor
in
CAD/CAM/CIM
. To promote flexibility and lifelong learning, students access
MOOCs via SWAYAM
and earn certifications.
The department has
state-of-the-art laboratories
, developed as per
AICTE guidelines
, supporting hands-on training and research. Over
₹2.5 crore
in research grants from reputed agencies have bolstered R&D and lab infrastructure. It also offers
consultancy services
in areas like vibration testing, material analysis, calibration, and CNC machining, generating
₹8–10 lakh annually
.
Active
student chapters of ASME, SAE, ASHRAE, and ISHRAE
conduct workshops and events. Students participate in competitions like
M-BAJA, E-BAJA, Efficycle, SUPRA, ACREX, and Go-Kart
, showcasing their technical skills.
The
Mechanical Engineering Students Association (MESA)
organizes co-curricular events, weekly club activities, and an annual state-level symposium
VERTEX
, promoting leadership, teamwork, and technical excellence.
Through the
TIFAC scheme
, students and faculty collaborate with MSMEs to offer technical solutions, enhancing industry-academia synergy. The
Rajiv Gandhi Science and Technology Commission (RGSTC)
supports applied research and innovation within the department.
Postgraduate students
undertake
dissertation work
at reputed companies like
DRDO, Dassault Systems, Cummins, HAL, Siemens, Thermax
, and others. The department recorded
100% placement of eligible students in 2024–25
, with graduates placed in core firms such as
Tata Motors, Atlas Copco, L&T, Mahindra, Eaton, Siemens Energy
, and software companies like
Infosys, TCS, and Cognizant
.
Students excel in
GATE, GRE, TOEFL, CAT, MPSC, and UPSC
, with many admitted to
IITs, NITs, IIMs
, and top global universities. Alumni hold senior roles in
ISRO, DRDO, HAL, L&T, Siemens, Infosys
, and others.
In essence, the department offers a balanced blend of theory, practice, and leadership development, preparing students for dynamic roles in engineering, research, and entrepreneurship while contributing meaningfully to society.
Objectives
The Department of Mechanical Science and Engineering aims to achieve the following objectives:
To prepare the students to excel in postgraduate programs or to succeed in industry/technical profession through global, rigorous Mechanical Engineering education.
To provide students with a sound foundation in Mathematics, Core Sciences and Mechanical Engineering fundamentals required to solve the problems in the field of Mechanical Engineering.
To train the students with good scientific and engineering breadth so as to comprehend, analyse, design and create novel products and give solutions for the real-life problems.
To inculcate in students professional, ethical attitude, effective communication skills, teamwork skills, multidisciplinary approach and ability to relate engineering issues to broader social context.
To provide students with an academic environment for excellence, leadership, managerial skills, written ethical codes and guidelines and lifelong learning needed for successful professional career.
To develop creativity, innovative ability and R&D culture to build new sustainable mechanisms, machines, systems and methodology for enhancing engineering and technology standards.
Policy
The Department of Mechanical Engineering is committed to upholding the highest standards of education, research, and professional integrity. Guided by its mission to foster excellence in mechanical engineering and technology.
Vision
To be a Mechanical Engineering Program of the first choice by the aspiring students and prospective employers by implementing world class education practices.
Mission
To meet the vision, all stakeholders of this programme are committed towards outcome based education philosophy by
Adopting vibrant academic curricula and implementing innovative teaching learning processes.
Providing opportunities to the students for the development of professional skills.
Nurturing critical thinking and creativity in students.
Inculcating in students the life-long learning attitude and sensitivity towards society and environment
Strength
The Department of Mechanical Engineering stands out for its key strengths, which include:
Experienced Faculty:
A team of highly qualified professors and industry experts specializing in key areas like Design, Thermal, Manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, and CAD/CAM/CAE, offering a strong mix of academic and industry knowledge.
Advanced Laboratories for Specialized Learning:
State-of-the-art labs equipped for Design, Thermal, and Manufacturing domains, enabling hands-on learning, simulations, and research.
Industry-Aligned Curriculum:
Curriculum regularly updated with the latest technologies and tools such as ANSYS, MATLAB, SolidWorks, and Autodesk, ensuring industry relevance.
Research and Innovation Culture:
Active involvement in funded projects, publications, and patents fosters innovation and provides real-world problem-solving opportunities.
Collaborations with Industry Leaders:
Strong ties with industries across automotive, aerospace, and manufacturing sectors offer internships, consultancy, and joint research opportunities.
Focused Skill Development Programs:
Workshops and training sessions in areas like CAD, FEA, CFD, Additive Manufacturing, and PLM to enhance technical competencies.
Strong Placement Record:
Consistent placements in top companies like Tata Motors, Mahindra, Siemens, and John Deere, along with opportunities in automation and renewable energy sectors.
Real-World Problem Solving through Industry Projects :
Students work on live, industry-sponsored projects, applying classroom learning to practical engineering challenges.
Dedicated Research Centers for Specialized Fields:
Centers focused on Thermal Systems, Product Design, and Advanced Manufacturing support high-level research and industrial collaborations.
Support for Innovation and Entrepreneurship:
Incubation centers and innovation clubs encourage start-ups and prototype development areas like sustainable systems and smart manufacturing.
Comprehensive Mentorship for Career Growth:
Faculty offer personalized guidance for research, career planning, and industry networking to prepare students for leadership roles.
Commitment to Excellence in Engineering Education:
Balanced focus on theory, practical skills, and innovation ensures graduates are industry-ready and socially responsible engineers.
Areas of Expertise
The Department of Mechanical Engineering excels in the following areas of expertise:
Design Engineering:
Focus on mechanical systems, machine elements, and innovative product design. Expertise includes FEA (ANSYS, Abaqus), vibration analysis, noise control, and PLM, ensuring reliable and optimized designs.
Thermal Engineering:
Strong in heat transfer, thermodynamics, and fluid mechanics, applied to IC engines, power plants, and heat exchangers. Proficient in CFD simulations and sustainable energy systems like solar, wind, and biomass.
Manufacturing Engineering:
Specialized in machining, casting, forming, CNC, and Additive Manufacturing. Focus on lean manufacturing, automation, and rapid prototyping to enhance precision and production efficiency.
Industrial Engineering:
Expertise in operations and supply chain management, lean systems, quality control, and ergonomics. Emphasis on productivity, safety, and sustainable process optimization.
CAD/CAM/CAE:
Advanced training in SolidWorks, AutoCAD, ANSYS, and MATLAB for design, simulation, and manufacturing. Strong in FEA, CFD, and structural analysis for high-quality product development.
Interdisciplinary Fields:
Combines robotics, mechatronics, automotive engineering, and materials science. Focus on smart systems, vehicle dynamics, EV technologies, and material optimization for diverse applications.
Salient Department Features
The
Department of Mechanical Engineering
at
Walchand College of Engineering
is distinguished by its commitment to academic excellence, innovation, and industry collaboration. The department stands out for its unique features and strengths:
Well-Equipped Laboratories :
Advanced labs in thermal, design, manufacturing, mechatronics, and materials science support hands-on learning and research.
Industry-Oriented Curriculum :
Regularly updated to reflect industry trends, with integrated simulations, case-based learning, and real-world applications.
Strong Research and Innovation Culture:
Active in core and interdisciplinary research with government and private funding; students contribute to impactful projects.
Focus on Project-Based Learning:
Embedded mini and final-year projects, along with innovation challenges, nurture problem-solving and application skills.
Hands-on Software Training:
Training in tools like ANSYS, SolidWorks, AutoCAD, MATLAB, and CREO equips students for technical roles in design and analysis.
Regular Industrial Visits and Internships:
Strong industry ties provide students with real-world exposure through visits, internships, and practical learning.
Active Student Chapters and Clubs:
Clubs like SAE, ISHRAE, ASME, and Robotics promote technical engagement and participation in national competitions.
Excellent Placement Support:
High placement rate across core, IT, and interdisciplinary sectors; training includes aptitude, soft skills, and technical prep.
Incubation and Entrepreneurship Support:
Support for start-up ideas through incubation facilities and mentoring for aspiring student entrepreneurs.
Alumni Network and Mentoring:
A strong alumni base actively guides students in academics, placements, and career development.
Focus on Sustainable and Green Technologies:
Research in renewable energy, waste-to-energy, and sustainable design aligns with global environmental goals.
Industry Sponsored Labs and MoUs with Industries:
Labs sponsored by companies like Siemens and PIL offer real-time tech exposure; MoUs strengthen academic-industry collaboration.
Industry-Supported Projects and Initiatives:
Through RGSTC and other initiatives, students work on live industry problems, gaining hands-on experience and practical skills.
Leadership
Dr. B. N. Naik
(Head of the Department  Mechanical Engineering)
A Warm Welcome to Aspiring Mechanical Engineers
Dr. Sagar U. Sapkal is a distinguished academician, researcher, and academic leader with over twenty-five years of experience in higher technical education. He currently serves as Professor and Head of the Department of Mechanical Engineering at Walchand College of Engineering. Dr. Sapkal earned his B.E. and M.E. in Mechanical Engineering from Walchand College of Engineering, Sangli, and completed his Ph.D. from Jadavpur University. His areas of specialization include Design Engineering, Advanced Manufacturing Systems, Industrial Engineering, Applied Operations Research, Optimization Techniques, and Additive Manufacturing. His research integrates analytical modeling and intelligent optimization approaches to address complex manufacturing and industrial engineering challenges.
An accomplished researcher, Dr. Sapkal has published 50 peer-reviewed journal papers and 48 conference papers at national and international forums. He has also contributed 2 book chapters and holds 6 patents, reflecting his strong orientation toward innovation and applied research. His scholarly impact is evidenced by 531 citations on Google Scholar, with an H-index of 11 and an i-10 index of 13, underscoring the relevance and influence of his research contributions. His work has been recognized with several awards, including the Best Paper Award at the International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Applications (ICAIA 2011) in Hong Kong, the Meritorious Prize at NAFEMS 2018 in Bengaluru, and the First Prize at IMTEX 2019 Academia Pavilion, Bengaluru.
Dr. Sapkal has an impressive record of research mentorship. He has guided 7 Ph.D. scholars (3 awarded, 1 submitted, and 3 ongoing), 42 M.Tech dissertations, and 32 B.Tech projects. He actively fostered innovation and entrepreneurship among students and served as a Mentor for Incubation initiatives in 3D Printing and Digital Prototyping Solutions, promoting technology-driven product development within the institution. He has also been associated with significant developmental and sponsored projects, including participation in the RGSTC–MSME scheme project and Engineering Design Internship Program, aimed at strengthening industry–institute collaboration and promoting technology transfer. He has actively represented the institution at international platforms, having attended and presented at conferences and seminars in Singapore, Hong Kong, and Austria. He has also served as a Jury Member for the Internal Smart India Hackathon, encouraging innovation, problem-solving, and interdisciplinary teamwork among students.
In his administrative capacity, Dr. Sapkal plays a pivotal role in academic planning, accreditation processes (NAAC/NBA), faculty development, and curriculum enhancement. As Head of the Department, he leads strategic initiatives for academic quality assurance and research promotion. He serves as Chairman of the Board of Studies (BoS) and Department Advisory Board (DAB), and contributes to academic governance through participation in various institutional committees.
He has significantly contributed to infrastructure development, including the establishment of Metrology & Manufacturing Technology Laboratories and the Product Innovation Laboratory. His efforts in strengthening industry interaction include consultancy projects, testing assignments, industrial visits, and MoU-driven academic and industry collaborations. He is a Life Member of ISTE and IIIE, a Life Fellow of IIPE, and a Member of ASME. His career reflects a balanced integration of academic scholarship, research innovation, administrative leadership, and commitment to institutional excellence.

Overview
Overview:  Department of Electrical Engineering
Through its long existence since 1955, Electrical Engineering Department of Walchand College of Engineering, Sangli has earned a great reputation and has become well known not only in our country, but also in the world through his alumni spread across the length and breadth of the globe. The Department was the second to be established in 1955 after Civil Engineering in 1947. Consequent to inception of the department, PG courses in two specializations, namely, Power System Engineering and Control System Engineering were started in the year 1971.
The Department offers a four-year course leading to the Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering (B. Tech.) and a two-year course leading to Master’s degree (M. Tech.) in Power System Engineering and Control System Engineering. Also, as a new initiative, there is provision for separate intake for working professionals with intake capacity of 30 students.
The Department has well-equipped laboratories, excellent computational facilities and software like MATLAB,  PSIM, Proteus, Keil, ETAP and AutoCAD – Electrical are available  to work on top-of-the-line projects in various areas of electrical engineering fields. The department has PLC and Automation lab with well-equipped Siemens PLC’s and VFD’s along with latest TIA software.
Department is a recognized research centre of Shivaji university of Kolhapur and also minor centre for QIP research scheme. Department also runs Ph. D. programme under AICTE Doctoral Fellowship (ADF) scheme.
The department has produced alumina working in many top industries like Siemens, General Electric TATA power, Adani Power, Bajaj, TATA motors, Atlas Copco and many more.
Objectives
The Department of Electrical Engineering aims to achieve the following objectives:
Provide Quality Education:
Deliver a comprehensive, industry-relevant curriculum to empower students with foundational knowledge, technical skills, and problem-solving abilities in the field of computer science and engineering.
Maintain Academic Excellence:
Continuously improve teaching methodologies, resources, and infrastructure to deliver a world-class educational experience that meets the highest academic standards.
Encourage Research and Innovation:
Promote a culture of research by encouraging students and faculty to explore emerging technologies, develop innovative solutions, and contribute to in core fields like Electrical machines, Power system, Control system and applications of advanced technologies like Artificial intelligence, machine learning applications in Electrical domain.
Developing practical, ethical and professional skills:
Enhancing student’s abilities to design, develop, and implement electrical systems and strong sense of ethical responsibility and professional conduct within the engineering field.
Connecting with industry and research organizations:
Promoting collaboration with industry partners and research organizations to bridge the gap between academic learning and practical applications as per industry requirements.
Encourage Lifelong Learning:
Encourage the importance of continuous learning and adaptability, preparing graduates to keep pace with the rapid evolution of technology and industry demands.
Strengthen Industry-Academia Collaboration:
Establish partnerships with leading companies and research organizations to provide students with exposure to real-world challenges, internships, placements, and collaborative projects.
Promote Entrepreneurship and Leadership:
Develop entrepreneurial skills and leadership qualities among students, inspiring them to create start-ups, lead teams, and innovate in the tech ecosystem.
Contribute to Society:
Develop socially responsible engineers by engaging students in projects and activities that address societal challenges, leveraging technology
Policy
The Department of Electrical Engineering is committed to maintain the high standards of education, research, and professional integrity. Guided by its mission to substitute excellence in computing and technology.
Vision
To be an Electrical Engineering program of the choice by the aspiring student and prospective employers by implementing world class education practices.
Mission
To implement Outcome Based Education Philosophy effectively by,
Adopting dynamic academic curricula and implementing innovative teaching learning process and research practices.
Providing opportunities to students for development of professional skills.
Nurturing critical thinking and creativity in the students.
Inculcate in the student’s life-long learning attitude and sensitivity towards society & environment.
Strength
The Department of Electrical Engineering stands out for its key strengths, which include:
Experienced and Dedicated Faculty
Industry oriented curriculum
Well-equipped labs with advanced machines and software’s
Research and Innovation
Strong Industry Connections
High Placement Record
Global Alumni Network
Good placement record
These strengths collectively position the department as a leader in Electrical Engineering education, research, and innovation.
Areas of Expertise
The Department of Electrical and Engineering excels in the following areas of expertise:
Electrical Power System – Operation and Control
Switchgear and Protection
Neural network and Fuzzy technology
Renewable Energy sources
Electric Vehicle Technology
Energy storage devices for EV
Power Electronics and Drives
Application of Power Electronics in Power System
Advanced Electrical Machines and Electrical machine design
Power Quality and Harmonics
Signal processing
These areas of expertise enable the department to provide students with advanced knowledge and practical skills, preparing them for leadership roles in the ever-evolving technology landscape.
Salient Department Features
The Department of Electrical and Engineering at Walchand College of Engineering stands out for its unique features and strengths, including:
Academic Excellence:
Industry-aligned curriculum focusing on foundational and advanced topics.
Highly qualified faculty with expertise in cutting-edge technologies. Nearly 40% of faculties awarded PhD and nearly 40% registered for PhD.
Well-equipped labs with advanced machines and software’s:
Modern electrical labs are equipped with high advanced electrical machines and equipment’s to meet the high standards of reputed industries.
The department has computer lab with latest high performing computers and access to advance software’s like MATLAB, ETAP, PSIM and Proteus etc.
Research and Innovation:
Active research in emerging fields like Electrical Power Systems, Power Quality, Electric Vehicle, Energy Management System and Battery Management Systems, etc.
Regular publications in reputed journals and conference participations with Scopus and SCI indexing.
Strong Industry Interface:
Collaborations with leading tech companies for internships, placements, and projects.
Industry-expert guest lectures, workshops, and certifications.
Skill Development Opportunities:
Emphasis on hands-on learning through hackathons, coding challenges, and projects.
Active technical clubs and student organizations fostering innovation.
Global Competence:
Alumni placed in top organizations and pursuing higher education globally.
Exposure to international competitions and exchange programs.
Student-Centric Environment:
Personalized mentoring by faculty for academic and professional growth.
Focus on holistic development through extracurricular and co-curricular activities.
Placement Excellence:
High placement rates with opportunities in top companies like Tata Power, Reliance Power, and IT Industries.
Dedicated training for technical interviews, coding tests, and soft skills.
Continuous Improvement:
Regular updates to the curriculum and teaching methodologies.
Feedback-driven enhancements for a superior learning experience.
Leadership
DR. VIJAY MOHALE
(PH.D. IIT ROORKEE)
Vijay Mohale (Senior Member, IEEE) is received his Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering and Master’s Degree in Electrical Power Systems from Shivaji University, Kolhapur, India, in 2011 and 2013, respectively. He completed his Doctoral Degree in the Power System Oscillation from the Power Electronics and Hydro-Electric Machines Laboratory at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Roorkee, India (2023). Currently, working as a Head of Electrical Department at Walchand College of Engineering, Sangli, India.
Dr. Mohale’s research interests include Power Systems Transients, Electromagnetic Compatibility, Sustainable Energy Transition, and Power Electronics for Renewable Grid Resilience. He has been granted Seven Indian Patents and Two Australian Patents. He is a Chartered Engineer and a Life Member of several professional organizations, including IEI, CMSI, IWRS, ISTE, and SPE. Recognized as a Postgraduate Teacher and a Research Supervisor for Ph.D. at Shivaji University, Kolhapur, Dr. Mohale actively contributes to both Academic and Industry-linked Research. He has made significant contributions to the field of Electrical Engineering through both Academic and Professional Interest. He received the IITR Travel Support to attend the 2021 IEEE IAS Annual Meeting held in Canada (October 10-14, 2021) and the CSIR Travel Support to participate in the 2022 IEEE IAS Annual Meeting in the USA (October 9-13, 2022) under Young Scientist Scheme. He has also been recognized as a Young Professional by IEEE for consecutive years, 2022 and 2023, in acknowledgment of his contributions.
Dr. Mohale’s commitment extends to hands-on learning, as he has arranged over 20 Industrial Visits to give Students practical insights into Industry Practices. He has also undertaken various Consultancy Projects, contributing his expertise in Energy Systems and Renewable Energy Applications to solve Real-World Industry Challenges. He is the author of the Book Power Electronics and Its Application, published by Khanna Publications, New Delhi and Steam Turbine in Thermal Power Plant – Practical Case Studies and Engineering Solutions accepted by CRC Press, Taylor & Francis. Dr. Mohale has presented his work at various prestigious International Conferences (27) and has published in reputed IEEE top tier Journals (5). He was awarded the Best Poster Award at the Institute Research Day (2022) at IIT Roorkee and the Best Paper Award at NIT Warangal (2024).

Overview: Department of Computer Science and Engineering
The Department of Computer Science and Engineering at Walchand College of Engineering (WCE), Sangli, established in 1986, is a pioneer in offering quality education in computing and IT. , head of the Computer Science and Engineering department, is an alumnus of the same institute. He completed his bachelor’s as well as his master’s in the Computer Department. His research publications include 29 papers in national/international conferences and 48 in international journals with more than 195 citations. He has filed four patents and three copyright. He has been actively instrumental in mentoring various workshops, conferences and student organizations with industry liaison. Keenly he has rolled out professional skill development training for the student community. He has delivered motivational sessions on pedagogy to nurture novel learning aspects in various engineering schools. Under his creative Transcend initiative, YouTube podcasts of star achievers success stories are revealed for juniors. Twelve years back he started SITAC (Social IT Awareness Campaign) initiative to raise awareness of the importance of IT for unprivileged school students through ACSES (Association of CSE Students) of Walchand college of engineering students’ volunteers. More than 14000 thousand school students and their respective teachers are benefitted by this social initiative. He is also proactively instrumental in extra-curricular activities & social initiatives for the unprivileged communities through WCE student fraternity.

Overview
Overview: Department of Information Technology
Information Technology (IT) Department was established in 2001 with an Under-Graduate (UG) programme and then Post Graduate (PG) was started in 2012. Both UG and PG programmes are NBA accredited. is the Head of the Department of Information Technology at Walchand College of Engineering, Sangli. Dr. Jahier Abbas Shaaikh
(Head of the Department of Robotics and Automation Engineering)
Dr. Jahier Abbas Shaaikh is a dedicated, result-oriented, and dynamic academic leader with over 19 years of teaching experience and 7 years of diverse industrial experience across the aerospace, defence manufacturing, compressor systems, and advanced engineering sectors. At WCE he has been instrumental in strengthening academic rigor, laboratory infrastructure, and the department’s strategic direction in emerging technologies.

Ltd., where he contributed to Akash Missile integration, defence production systems, and aerospace component manufacturing. Tech research projects both in India and abroad. Dr. Shaaikh has a strong interest in Design Thinking with Aerospace Manufacturing, leveraging it as a structured methodology to drive innovation in product development, engineering design, and problem-solving frameworks.
