Overview
Overview: Department of Design
The Bachelor of Design (B.Des.) programme is a four-year undergraduate degree designed to cultivate creativity, critical thinking, problem-solving abilities, and professional competence through a balanced blend of design theory, studio-based learning, design fundamentals integrated with engineering and technology, and experiential practice. The programme emphasizes the creation of meaningful products, systems, services, and experiences that enhance the quality of life while addressing real-world challenges across diverse domains such as industrial products, digital interfaces, mobility, healthcare, consumer products, smart technologies, public systems, and sustainable development.
Industry engagement forms an integral component of the programme through expert lectures, live design projects, internships, field studies, collaborative workshops, portfolio development, and interaction with professionals from industry, academia, and the entrepreneurial ecosystem. Students are encouraged to participate in innovation challenges, design competitions, research activities, incubation initiatives, and community-centric projects that promote creativity, leadership, teamwork, and lifelong learning.
The Department is committed to fostering an inclusive academic environment that values originality, ethical practice, sustainability, and social responsibility. Graduates of the programme will be prepared to contribute as competent design professionals, innovators,
entrepreneurs, researchers, and future leaders capable of developing impactful solutions that address the needs of individuals, industries, and society at large.
Through its unique integration of design excellence, engineering knowledge, technological innovation, and human-centred creativity, the Department of Design at Walchand College of Engineering aspires to emerge as a centre of excellence in design education, empowering
students to shape products, services, systems, and experiences that create lasting value for society and contribute meaningfully to national and global development.
Programme Positioning
The B.Des. programme at Walchand College of Engineering is positioned at the intersection of Design, Engineering, Technology, Business and Society. The programme combines human-centred design with engineering knowledge, digital technologies, emerging technologies, entrepreneurship and real-world problem solving. Students are prepared not only to create products and experiences, but also to design services, systems, business opportunities and innovative solutions that can be implemented and scaled across industry and society.
Design Programme - Everything You Need to Know at Walchand College of Engineering, Sangli.
Objectives
Professional Competence
Demonstrate proficiency in applying design thinking, creativity, engineering fundamentals, and contemporary design methodologies to develop innovative, user-centred, and sustainable solutions for products, systems, services, and experiences.
Innovation and Problem Solving
Analyze complex societal, industrial, and technological challenges, and develop effective design solutions through research, critical thinking, experimentation, interdisciplinary collaboration, and evidence-based decision-making.
Professional Practice and Leadership
Excel as competent design professionals, entrepreneurs, researchers, or innovators by exhibiting leadership, effective communication, teamwork, project management, and professional ethics in multidisciplinary and multicultural environments.
Technology Integration and Lifelong Learning
Adapt to emerging technologies, digital design tools, advanced manufacturing, artificial intelligence, and evolving design practices through continuous learning, higher education, professional development, and research.
Sustainability and Social Responsibility
Design products, systems, and experiences that are environmentally sustainable, socially responsible, economically viable, and inclusive, while adhering to ethical, legal, and professional standards.
Industry and Global Readiness
Contribute effectively to industry, academia, startups, and the global design ecosystem by demonstrating adaptability, innovation, entrepreneurial mindset, and a commitment to quality, continuous improvement, and lifelong learning.
Graduate Attributes
Graduates of the programme will demonstrate creative and critical thinking, human-centred research capabilities, design and prototyping skills, technological fluency, interdisciplinary collaboration, communication and leadership, entrepreneurial thinking, professional ethics, sustainability consciousness and the ability to translate design concepts into viable products, services, systems and experiences.
Policy
The Department of Design is committed to delivering quality design education through
Outcome-Based Education, fostering creativity, innovation, interdisciplinary learning, ethical
values, and continuous improvement to develop globally relevant and socially responsible
design professionals.
Vision
To be a centre of excellence in design education by nurturing creative, innovative, and
ethically responsible designers capable of developing sustainable, human-centred solutions
for society and industry through creativity, innovation and technology.
Mission
To impart multidisciplinary, learner-centric design education through Outcome-Based
Education by fostering creativity, innovation, industry collaboration, ethics, and lifelong
learning to develop competent professionals for sustainable and human-centred design.
Programme Philosophy
The programme follows a Learn–Make–Test–Reflect–Implement philosophy, where learning
moves continuously between theory, observation, experimentation, making, technology, user
interaction and real-world implementation. Studio-based learning is complemented by
interdisciplinary projects, industry engagement, field research, prototyping, entrepreneurship
and reflective practice.
Strengths of the Department
A distinctive strength of the programme is its studio-based and project-oriented pedagogy, where students learn through observation, exploration, ideation, prototyping, testing, and iterative refinement. Real-world design challenges, collaborative projects, case studies, workshops, and design reviews encourage critical thinking, innovation, teamwork, and effective communication while fostering an entrepreneurial mindset.
The Department leverages WCE’s well-established academic infrastructure, including advanced laboratories, workshops, digital design facilities, prototyping resources, computing facilities, and the central library, providing students with a strong foundation for experiential learning and design innovation. Strong industry engagement through internships, live projects, expert interactions, workshops, industrial visits, and collaborative activities enhances practical exposure and professional readiness. The Department also fosters innovation, research, and entrepreneurship by encouraging participation in design competitions, research projects, and incubation initiatives. Emphasis on ethics, sustainability, inclusivity, and social responsibility enables students to develop human-centred design solutions that create meaningful impact for industry and society.
Design Innovation Ecosystem
The Department will function as an interdisciplinary design innovation ecosystem connecting students and faculty with engineering disciplines, industry, startups, researchers, entrepreneurs, alumni, government and communities. The ecosystem will facilitate live
projects, design challenges, research, prototyping, internships, innovation programmes, intellectual property creation and venture development, enabling students to work on real problems and create measurable impact.
Salient Department Features
Multidisciplinary Learning
Integrates design with engineering, technology, management, and applied sciences to foster
holistic problem-solving.
Studio-Based Learning
Emphasizes experiential learning through design studios, projects, prototyping, workshops,
and collaborative activities.
Design Thinking & Innovation
Encourages creativity, user-centred design, critical thinking, and innovative approaches to
solving real-world challenges.
Indian Context & Social Innovation
Design exploration of Indian social, cultural, industrial and environmental challenges through inclusive design, frugal innovation, local knowledge, crafts and community-centred innovation.
State-of-the-art Design Studios and Prototyping Facilities
Access to advanced laboratories, workshops, digital design tools, prototyping facilities, computing resources, and innovation ecosystem.
Industry Collaboration
Industry internships, live projects, expert lectures, industrial visits, and collaborative programmes enhance professional exposure and employability.
Design Entrepreneurship & Commercialisation
Learning to transform design opportunities into viable products, services and ventures through business models, intellectual property, branding, costing, market validation and go-to-market strategies. Opportunities for innovation, intellectual property creation, startup incubation, and participation in national design and startup competitions, hackathons, projects calls, etc.
Research & Systems Thinking
Development of capabilities in qualitative and quantitative research, systems thinking, service design, strategic design and complex problem solving.
Technology-Enabled Design
Exposure to emerging technologies such as AI, IoT, AR/VR, digital fabrication, smart manufacturing, and human-computer interaction. Exposure to generative design, computational creativity, AI-assisted research, human–AI interaction and emerging digital tools.
Sustainability & Social Responsibility
Focus on inclusive, ethical, environmentally responsible, and human-centred design for societal impact.
Professional Development
Portfolio development, communication skills, leadership, teamwork, and lifelong learning
prepare graduates for global careers and higher education.
Global Design Exposure
International design challenges, global industry interactions, academic collaborations, visiting
faculty, exchange opportunities and exposure to global design practices.
Programme and Curriculum Architecture
Common Design Core
All students undertake a common interdisciplinary design foundation covering design research, human-centred design, design thinking, visual communication, materials and making, technology, sustainability, systems thinking, entrepreneurship and professional practice before progressing into their chosen specialisation.
The B.Des. programme offers four distinct specialization tracks tailored to modern industry needs.

Overview
Overview: Department of Humanities and Sciences
Department of Humanities and Sciences
The Department of Humanities and Sciences at Walchand College of Engineering, Sangli, plays a pivotal role in providing a strong foundational education that complements the technical disciplines. It equips students with critical thinking, communication skills, and interdisciplinary knowledge essential for well-rounded engineers.
Academic Courses
The department offers a diverse range of courses designed to build a solid scientific and humanistic foundation for engineering students. These include:
Engineering Physics, Engineering Chemistry, Engineering Mathematics, English, Biology for Engineers, Accounts and Finance, Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS) etc.
Role in Holistic Development
The department emphasizes critical thinking, ethical values, and interdisciplinary learning. Through courses like English and IKS, students develop communication skills and cultural awareness, while science and mathematics courses build analytical rigor. Faculty members mentor students to integrate these skills into their technical education, preparing them for leadership roles.
Infrastructure and Resources
The department is supported by:
Well-equipped laboratories for physics, chemistry, and language lab.
A rich library with resources in sciences, humanities, and interdisciplinary studies.
Achievements:
Students excel in interdisciplinary competitions and projects, leveraging their foundational knowledge.
Objectives
The Department of Humanities and Sciences at WCE, Sangli, aims to lay a strong interdisciplinary foundation for engineering students, promoting holistic development through the following objectives:
Provide Foundational Education:
Deliver high-quality courses in Engineering Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, English, Biology for Engineers, Accounts and Finance, Biotechnology, and Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS) to build a solid scientific and humanistic base for engineering applications.
Enhance Critical Thinking and Communication:
Develop students’ analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills through courses like English and Mathematics, preparing them for professional and leadership roles.
Foster Lifelong Learning:
Cultivate an appreciation for continuous learning in sciences and humanities, enabling students to adapt to interdisciplinary challenges in their careers.
Encourage Ethical and Cultural Awareness:
Promote ethical values and cultural understanding through courses like IKS, fostering socially responsible engineers with a global perspective.
Maintain Academic Rigor:
Continuously improve teaching practices, laboratory facilities, and resources to provide a world-class foundational education that complements technical disciplines.
Vision
To build a strong academic foundation for engineering students through integrated knowledge in science, mathematics, communication, and values, fostering research orientation, leadership, and holistic development in line with the institute’s vision.
Mission
To impart fundamental scientific, mathematical, and communication skills necessary for engineering education and innovation.
To nurture ethical reasoning, environmental awareness, and cultural understanding through value-based education.
To support interdisciplinary learning through well-structured open elective and skill-enhancement courses.
To develop scientific temper, creativity, and analytical thinking among students for solving real-world problems.
To inculcate in the student’s life-long learning attitude and sensitivity towards
society & environment. To create a vibrant academic environment through mentor              mentee support, modern pedagogy, and continuous faculty development.
Quality Policy
The Humanities and Science Department is committed to:
Delivering quality education through outcome-based teaching methodologies and continuous improvement in curriculum.
Encouraging research, innovation, and value-based learning through updated pedagogical tools and interactive platforms.
Promoting interdisciplinary learning by offering a wide spectrum of electives aligned with emerging technological and social needs.
Providing a supportive academic ecosystem through mentoring, performance monitoring, and individual counselling.
Ensuring continual enhancement of infrastructure, faculty competence, and student engagement to meet global standards in engineering education.
Leadership
Prof. Anil Anandrao Powar
(Head of the Department of Humanities and Sciences )
Prof. Anil Anandrao Powar is the Head of the Department of Humanities and Sciences at Walchand College of Engineering (WCE), Sangli.
His research interests include nanomaterials, electrochemical sensors, and gas sensing applications. Prof. Powar has authored & co-authored several publications in high-impact international journals, such as Journal of Materials Science: Materials in Electronics and RSC Advances. Notable works include the synthesis of TiO2-ZnO-BMIMBr nanocomposites for neurotransmitter sensing and perovskites for supercapacitor applications. He has also presented papers at national and international conferences, including topics like outcome-based education and nanotechnology.
Prof. Powar has been actively involved in administrative roles, including First-Year Coordinator (2006–2010), Examination Coordinator (2010–2011), and Admission Committee member (1996–2008). He has served as ARC In-Charge/Counsellor for admissions since 2010 and provided counselling to over 40,000 students and parents across India and abroad for the past 29 years. Additionally, he established and managed the WCE Student Health Centre (2008–2011, 2016), Worked for 6 Sub-liaison officer CET examination and Sub nodel officer twice for MHT CET  and contributed to voter registration drives for students.
He has received numerous accolades, including the Excellent Faculty of the Year award 2023–24 by Saksham Society, Bhartia Guru Gaurav Samman 2024 by Uttdhan Foundation, and Maulana Abdul Kalam Azad Education Award 2024 for outstanding contributions to education. Prof. Powar is a Life Member of the Indian Society for Technical Education (ISTE) and holds memberships in professional bodies.
Prof. Powar’s dedication to education, research, and community service has established him as a respected leader in the academic and social spheres at Walchand College of Engineering.

At Walchand College of Engineering (WCE), we believe that education should be a transformative experience that fosters intellectual curiosity, creativity, and critical thinking. Our curriculum is designed to provide students with a comprehensive education that prepares them for successful careers and lifelong learning.
Curriculum Structure
The WCE curriculum is structured across multiple academic years, each year consisting of two semesters. This structure allows for a balanced and progressive learning experience, with each semester building on the previous one.
Mandatory Courses
Mandatory courses form the core of our curriculum, providing students with a solid foundation in their chosen discipline. These courses are designed to ensure that students acquire essential knowledge, skills, and competencies.
Elective Courses
Elective courses offer students the flexibility to explore their interests and passions, while also broadening their knowledge and skills. These courses are designed to provide students with a deeper understanding of specific topics and their applications.
Teaching-Learning Methodology
Apart from classroom expert lectures, experiential learning is enabled through hands-on sessions in Labs, field work,  project works and internships. Each course is assigned credits, as a measure of learning effort expected to be invested by students.
Classroom Expert Lectures
Classroom expert lectures provide students with a comprehensive introduction to key concepts, theories, and principles. Our faculty members are experts in their fields, and their lectures are designed to engage, inspire, and challenge students.
Hands-on Sessions in Labs
Hands-on sessions in labs provide students with the opportunity to apply theoretical knowledge in a practical setting. Our state-of-the-art labs are equipped with the latest equipment and software, allowing students to experiment, innovate, and learn through direct experience.
Field Work
Field work provides students with the opportunity to apply theoretical knowledge in real-world settings. Our field work programs are designed to provide students with hands-on experience, allowing them to develop practical skills, observe phenomena, and collect data.
Project Works
Project works provide students with the opportunity to integrate theoretical knowledge with practical skills, working on real-world problems and applications. Our project works are designed to foster creativity, innovation, and critical thinking, while also developing essential skills in teamwork, communication, and problem-solving.
Internships
Internships provide students with the opportunity to gain practical experience in industry, applying theoretical knowledge in real-world settings. Our internship programs are designed to provide students with hands-on experience, allowing them to develop practical skills, build professional networks, and enhance their employability.
Philosophy of Outcome-Based Education (OBE)
Outcome-Based Education (OBE) is a student-centered approach to education that focuses on measuring student learning outcomes, rather than just teaching inputs. The philosophy of OBE is based on the following principles:
Student-Centered Learning: OBE places the student at the center of the learning process, emphasizing their active participation and engagement in achieving learning outcomes.
Clear Learning Outcomes: OBE requires clear and specific learning outcomes that are aligned with the program’s educational objectives.
Measurable Learning Outcomes: OBE emphasizes the importance of measuring student learning outcomes, using a range of assessment methods to evaluate student performance.
Continuous Improvement: OBE encourages continuous improvement, using data and feedback from students, faculty, and employers to refine and improve the curriculum.
Bloom's Taxonomy
WCE has incorporated Bloom’s Taxonomy in our teaching learning practices.
Bloom’s Taxonomy provides a structured approach to designing learning objectives, ensuring that students are challenged to think critically and solve complex problems.
Bloom’s Taxonomy is a framework for categorizing learning objectives into six levels of cognitive complexity:
Remembering: Recall previously learned information.
Understanding: Comprehend the meaning of learned information.
Applying: Use learned information to solve problems or complete tasks.
Analyzing: Break down complex information into component parts.
Evaluating: Make judgments about the value or quality of information.
Creating: Generate new ideas, products, or solutions.
Pedagogy
WCE has developed one of finest Pedagogy for stundents’ learning. Effective pedagogy involves creating a supportive learning environment that encourages student engagement, motivation, and learning.
Some key principles of WCE effective pedagogy include:
Student-Centered Learning: Encourage student participation, engagement, and autonomy in the learning process.
Active Learning: Incorporate activities, discussions, and problem-solving exercises to promote active learning.
Differentiation: Recognize and respond to the diverse needs and abilities of students.
Feedback: Provide regular, constructive feedback to students to support their learning and development.
Reflection: Encourage students to reflect on their learning, setting goals and identifying areas for improvement.

Flipped Classroom: Reverse the traditional lecture-homework format, delivering instructional content at home and working on activities and projects in the classroom.

Credit System and Bank
Credit System and Bank
The WCE curriculum is structured across multiple academic years, each year consisting of two semesters, and includes a mix of mandatory and elective courses. Apart from classroom expert lectures, experiential learning is enabled through hands-on sessions in Labs, field work,  project works and internships. Each course is assigned credits, as a measure of learning effort expected to be invested by students.
Typically, one credit is assigned for one hour of instruction per week through lectures or tutorials. For laboratory sessions, mini-projects, or seminars, one credit is awarded for every two hours of student engagement per week. For undergraduate students admitted in the academic year 2023-24 and beyond, 174 credits must be earned to obtain a Bachelor’s degree in an Engineering discipline with a Multi-Disciplinary Minor. Whereas for earning a Masters one need to earn 80 credits in the span of minimum four semesters.
WCE follows a choice-based credit system, offering partial flexibility within its autonomous academic programs. Students can select courses from a range of Open Electives, Multi-Disciplinary streams, and Program Electives. Students may select the best courses or combination of courses to suit their aptitude and quest for knowledge.
Additionally, WCE is part of the Academic Bank of Credit (ABC) system, launched by the Government of India. As a result, these credits are digitally recorded in unique student accounts, which are recognized nationwide. All academic credits earned through WCE, partnering institutes and online approved platforms are stored, acknowledged, maintained, accumulated, transferred, validated, and can be redeemed for the purpose of degree certification.

Academic Regulations
Academic Regulations
Walchand College of Engineering (WCE) follows a comprehensive set of academic regulations designed to aid in the ecosystem to achieve learning goals.
Continuous assessment philosophy is implemented to allow stakeholders to assess the progress in learning.  The theory course is assessed through ISE (20 marks
), MSE(30 marks) and ESE (50Marks). A passing criterion is that a minimum of  40% marks be achieved overall and also in ESE. (Abbreviations – ISE – In Semester Examination , MSE – Mid Semester Examination , ESE – End  Semester Examination )
Marks are translated into alphabetic grades using the relative grading system which rationalizes variation in marks. Grades obtained in all courses in a semester are assimilated with due respect to respective credit weights to compute the Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) on a scale of 0 to 10. As students progress through multiple semesters, the Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) is updated along with total number of credits earned to reflect both quantity and quality of learning achievements. For undergraduate students admitted in the academic year 2023-24 and beyond, 174 credits must be earned to obtain a Bachelor’s degree in an Engineering discipline with a Multi-Disciplinary Minor.
To be promoted to the next academic year learners must attain at least two-thirds of the credits designated for the completed academic year. This system emphasizes academic rigor and aims to ensure that students possess a strong foundation in their chosen field of study before advancing to higher levels of education.
Attendance is a crucial component of these regulations, with students required to maintain a minimum attendance of 75% in lectures of theory courses. In performance-based courses, attendance is one of the mandatory criteria to be eligible for examinations. In case of medical or personal emergencies, students must provide valid documentation to seek exemptions or relaxations, subject to the approval of the authorities. If a student defaults in three or more courses in a semester, a detention is thrust upon him/her. The institute discourages malpractices in the examination through various inbuilt preventive measures. However, in case of such an event, an empowered committee cancels the student’s performance in that course or detains student for whole semester too.

Overview
Overview: Department of Civil Engineering
Objectives
To provide students with fundamental knowledge and practical skills
in Civil Engineering for planning, surveying, construction, testing, maintenance, and supervision of engineering works.
To develop technically competent diploma engineers
capable of assisting in the execution, operation, and maintenance of civil engineering projects while following established engineering practices and standards.
To inculcate professional ethics, discipline, leadership, and teamwork
, enabling graduates to work responsibly and effectively in multidisciplinary environments.
To prepare diploma graduates to meet the needs of society
by contributing to the development, maintenance, and sustainability of civil infrastructure with due consideration for safety and environmental protection.
To encourage lifelong learning and professional growth
through higher education, skill development, certification programs, and adaptation to emerging technologies in Civil Engineering.
To develop effective communication, problem-solving, and interpersonal skills
that enable graduates to interact professionally with clients, contractors, government agencies, and the community.
Vision
To be an excellent Civil Engineering programme of first choice to meet ever-growing needs of society.
Mission
M 1: Adoption and implementation of excellent effective teaching- Learning, with focus on social and environmentally friendly problem solutions.
M 2: Motivating students to work with emerging and diversified technologies in line with industrial practices.
M 3: Inculcating excellent professional skills required for project management and lifelong learning.

Leadership
Mr. H. P. KULKARNI
Head, Department of Civil Engineering  (Polytechnic Wing)
He is a postgraduate Civil Engineer with a specialization in
Town and Country Planning
from
College of Engineering Pune (CoEP)
. He has over
30 years of professional experience
, including 25 years in teaching and academic administration and 5 years in industry.
He has been associated with this institute as a
faculty member and Head of the Department (HoD) since 2017
, contributing extensively to the academic and institutional development of the department through teaching, administration, and academic leadership. He also served as the
Chairperson of the General Maintenance Committee, Walchand College of Engineering (WCE), for two years
.
Prior to joining WCE, he served at
Govt. Polytechnic-Kolhapur, CIDCO
Navi Mumbai
,
Bharati Vidyapeeth,
and
Vishwakarma Institutes
at Pune. He is a
Dale Carnegie Certified High Impact Presenter
, an
IRCA-Certified Lead Auditor for Quality Management Systems (QMS)
, and an
ESCI–QCI Certified Management Representative (M.R.) for ISO 9001
.
His areas of academic and professional interest include
Engineering Mechanics, Building Materials and Construction, Building Planning, Construction Management, Surveying, and Urban Planning
.
He has undertaken and contributed to several academic and professional assignments of
Savitribai Phule Pune University (SPPU), Pune
, and the

. He is also involved in consultancy services related to various
civil engineering projects
.
He is a ‘

and an ‘
Associate Member’ of the Institute of Town Planners, India
.
Under his academic leadership, the
Department of Civil Engineering (P.W.) was recently accredited by the National Board of Accreditation (NBA)
, marking a significant achievement in the department’s pursuit of academic excellence and quality enhancement.

Student Careers
WCE is  dedicated to fostering the comprehensive development of our students, with a focus on Students’ career, their employability, entrepreneurship abilities , higher education and professional development.  This is achieved through our Transformational Teaching Learning (TTL) processes, which include a Track-Based Curriculum and a Choice- Based Credit System, in addition to a range of Value-Added Professional and Life Skill Courses. These initiatives enable students to chart a clear path towards their chosen career.
The graduates of WCE are highly sought after by prestigious multinational and Indian companies including Rubrik, CRED, Google, Microsoft Inc., Adobe, Amazon, Coinswitch, Wayfair, Cadence Design Systems, Deutsche Bank, Tessell Inc., Applied Materials, Gupshup Technologies, Druva Inc., TOM TOM Intl., UBS Business Solutions, BMC Software’s, NVIDIA and many others. WCE students are frequently offered substantial compensation packages,
Many of WCE students have successfully established their own enterprises and shown extraordinary entrepreneurship abilities. Many successful business brands are owned by WCE ammeters
Similarly, many alumni have chosen government jobs for serving in public services. And many of them have pursued MTech, MS, MBA , PhD and successfully fulfilled their aspiration for higher / highest qualifications
At WCE, we recognize the importance of career development and placement support for our students. The Career Development Cell (CDC) is a dedicated team that works tirelessly to provide comprehensive career guidance, training, and placement opportunities to our students.

Career Development Cell
Carrer Development Cell
The current global landscape calls for engineers who possess a unique combination of technical proficiency, creative thinking, and quick problem-solving abilities. With the advent of advanced academic programs and institutes of higher learning, as well as students seeking to diversify their skill set and explore new career avenues, the Career Development Cell at the institution is poised to effectively lead students to success
The job market is highly competitive, and in order to remain relevant, students and newly graduated engineers must possess advanced technical skills. Many students aim to achieve this by pursuing higher education from prestigious Indian Institutes or foreign universities or by scoring excellent marks in standardized technical exams. Others want to advance their careers by serving the government and in order to achieve this, they need to ace civil service and army exams. Most importantly, this cell serves as an aid for students to find their passions, experiment with career alternatives, and acquire knowledge. It provides support for students who are considering a change in their major track by offering guidance and aid. The cell acts as a central point for students to investigate, get information about exams and job opportunities, and connect with others who share similar interests.
Mission
The mission of the Career Development Cell is to empower students with the skills, knowledge, and networking opportunities necessary to succeed in their chosen careers. We strive to foster strong relationships with industry partners, alumni, and other stakeholders to provide our students with a competitive edge in the job market.
CDC functions
To offer students, from all domains, with quality career opportunities via  placements from a large number of core companies, product-based companies, service-based industries and research-oriented companies.
Provide career guidance and counseling to students
To provide good industry associations and connections.
To Organize training programs, workshops, and seminars to enhance employability skills
To Facilitate internships, projects opportunities for students
To Coordinate placement drives, recruitment events, and job fairs
To  Foster relationships with industry partners, alumni, and other stakeholders
To  Provide resources and support for higher education and research pursuit
To establish and maintain alumni connections with industry and academic distinctions.
To harness the expertise of successful alumni, who work in a diverse range of fields, to provide guidance to students seeking a variety of career paths.
To facilitate the student’s understanding of their interests and aptitudes – by organizing expert sessions on various topics and domains.
To enable the student to undertake a self-evaluation of their competencies.
To organize various employability trainings , ensure student aptitude , logic is developed
To incorporate logic, aptitude , and other skills in curriculum structure
To help the student chart their career path, based on their interests and aptitude, and provide support in determining the necessary exams to succeed in their chosen field.
To divide the students into one of three skills, each focusing on a particular set of standard exams.
To provide information and guidance on patterns of assessments  and frequently asked questions.
To build a self-sustaining community of learners who are keen on collaborating and working together to achieve success in the standardized national and international exams

Placement in WCE
Placement in WCE
WCE has a strong reputation for providing excellent placement opportunities to its students. The college has a dedicated placement cell that works tirelessly to ensure that students are placed in top companies across various industries.
WCE has a strong placement record, with a high placement percentage, top recruiters, and high salary packages. The college provides various placement support services to enhance students’ employability skills and help them secure their dream jobs.
The Career Development Cell  encompasses a Placement activity and is  be responsible for establishing connections with industries and companies across various domains and sectors, inviting them to participate in on-campus placement activities. The cell  strive to maintain strong relationships with HRs and senior executives, and organize industry meets and seminars in partnership with these companies. These initiatives  provide students with the chance to engage with industry professionals, enabling them to construct their professional profiles in line with current industry trends and demands.
Functions
Inviting Companies:
Inviting top companies to campus for recruitment.
Student Preparation:
Preparing students for placements through training programs, workshops, and seminars.
Placement Process:
Coordinating the placement process, including written tests, group discussions, and personal interviews.
Placement Statistics:
Maintaining placement statistics and analyzing trends to improve placement outcomes.
Placement Process
The placement process at WCE typically involves the following steps:
Company Registration:
Companies register with the placement cell to participate in the placement process.
Job Description:
Companies provide job descriptions, including job roles, responsibilities, and requirements.
Student Registration:
Students register for placements, providing their resume, academic records, and other relevant documents.
Shortlisting:
Companies shortlist students based on their resume, academic records, and other criteria.
Online /Written Test /Contests:
Shortlisted students appear for a Online /Written Test /Contests, which may include aptitude tests, technical tests, or both.
Group Discussion:
Students who clear the written test participate in a group discussion, which assesses their communication skills, teamwork, and problem-solving abilities.
Personal Interview:
Students who clear the group discussion participate in a personal interview, which assesses their technical skills, personality, and fit with the company culture.

Internships
Internships
Internships provide students with invaluable hands-on experience, industry exposure, and networking opportunities. Internships are a crucial component of engineering studies, providing students with hands-on experience, industry exposure, and networking opportunities.
At Walchand College of Engineering (WCE), internships are highly valued as they enable students to apply theoretical concepts to real-world problems, develop practical skills, and enhance their employability. We facilitate internships, projects, and research opportunities for students in collaboration with industry partners, research institutions, and startups.
Why Internships are Required
Internships are essential for engineering students as they:
Bridge the gap between theory and practice:
Internships provide students with hands-on experience, enabling them to apply theoretical concepts to real-world problems.
Develop practical skills:
Internships help students develop essential skills such as problem-solving, communication, teamwork, and time management.
Enhance employability:
Internships provide students with industry exposure, networking opportunities, and a chance to build relationships with potential employers.
Prepare students for final-year projects*:
Internships help students develop research skills, identify project topics, and gather data, which can be useful for their final-year projects.
Types of Internships
WCE offers various types of internships to cater to different student needs and interests:
Summer Internships:
4-8 weeks internships during summer vacations.
Winter Internships:
4-8 weeks internships during winter vacations.
Long-term Internships:
6 months to 1-year internships, which can be pursued during the final year of studies.
Research Internships:
Internships focused on research projects, which can be pursued during the final year of studies.
Boot camps:
This is skilling activities cum internship . sometimes housed in college.
Benefits of Internships
Internships offer numerous benefits to students, including:
Stipend:
Many companies offer stipends to interns, which can help students cover living expenses.
Assessment and Feedback:
Interns receive regular assessment and feedback from supervisors, which helps them improve their skills and performance.
Networking Opportunities:

Higher Education
After completing their undergraduate studies in engineering, many students aspire to pursue higher education to enhance their knowledge, skills, and career prospects. This note provides an overview of various higher education options, including MBA, MTech, MS, and global PG studies.  At Walchand College of Engineering (WCE), we recognize the importance of higher education in enhancing career prospects, developing specialized knowledge and skills, and fostering personal growth. For students aspiring to pursue higher education, we provide guidance and support on various aspects. Higher education can lead to better job opportunities, higher salaries, and faster career growth.
Specialized knowledge and skills:
Higher education provides students with specialized knowledge and skills in their chosen field
Networking opportunities:

Personal growth and development:
Higher education can lead to personal growth and development, including improved critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication skills.

Identifying suitable universities and programs
Preparing for entrance exams and interviews

Preparing Students for Higher Education
MBA through CAT
What is CAT?_: The Common Admission Test (CAT) is a national-level entrance exam conducted by the Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs) for admission to MBA programs.
Eligibility: Bachelor’s degree with at least 50% marks or equivalent CGPA.
Preparation: CAT preparation involves developing skills in areas like quantitative ability, verbal ability, and logical reasoning.
IIMs and other top B-schools_: IIM Ahmedabad, IIM Bangalore, IIM Calcutta, IIM Lucknow, and other top B-schools like XLRI, FMS, and MDI.
CAT Preparation
We provide guidance and support to students preparing for the Common Admission Test (CAT) for admission to MBA programs at top B-schools like IIMs.
Our faculty members and industry experts conduct workshops, seminars, and coaching sessions to help students develop the required skills and knowledge.
MTech through GATE
What is GATE?: The Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering (GATE) is a national-level entrance exam conducted jointly by the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) and the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) for admission to MTech programs.
Eligibility
: Bachelor’s degree in engineering or technology with at least 50% marks or equivalent CGPA.
Preparation
: GATE preparation involves developing skills in areas like engineering mathematics, general aptitude, and subject-specific knowledge.
Top institutes:
IITs, NITs, and other top engineering institutes.
GATE Preparation
We offer guidance and support to students preparing for the Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering (GATE) for admission to MTech programs at top institutes like IITs and NITs.
Our faculty members and industry experts conduct workshops, seminars, and coaching sessions to help students develop the required skills and knowledge.
MS and Global PG Studies
What is GRE?
: The Graduate Record Examinations (GRE) is a standardized test required for admission to graduate schools in the United States and other countries.
What is TOEFL:
The Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) is a standardized test required for admission to graduate schools in the United States and other English-speaking countries.
Eligibility:
Bachelor’s degree with at least 50% marks or equivalent CGPA.
Preparation:
GRE and TOEFL preparation involves developing skills in areas like verbal reasoning, quantitative reasoning, and analytical writing.

United States:
Top universities like Stanford, MIT, UC Berkeley, and Harvard.
Canada :
Top universities like University of Toronto, University of British Columbia, and McGill University.
Europe:
Top universities like University of Oxford, University of Cambridge, ETH Zurich, and École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL).
Australia:
Top universities like University of Melbourne, University of Sydney, and Australian National University (ANU).
GRE and TOEFL Preparation
We provide guidance and support to students preparing for the Graduate Record Examinations (GRE) and Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) for admission to MS and global PG programs.
Our faculty members and industry experts conduct workshops, seminars, and coaching sessions to help students develop the required skills and knowledge.

We facilitate one-on-one counselling sessions to students to help them choose the right higher education program and institution.
Our counselors provide guidance on the application process, including resume building, statement of purpose, and letter of recommendation.

Innovation/IIE Cell
Overview
Innovation Cell is a platform that fosters innovation, entrepreneurship, and creativity among students, faculty, and staff. The primary objective of the Innovation Cell is to encourage and support innovative ideas, provide resources and mentorship, and facilitate collaboration between academia and industry.
Walchand College of Engineering (WCE) has established an Innovation Cell to foster innovation, entrepreneurship, and creativity among students, faculty, and staff. The Innovation Cell at WCE aims to provide a platform for students and faculty to develop and refine their innovative ideas, provide resources and mentorship, and facilitate collaboration between academia and industry. WCE has also been ranked among the top institutions in the country in the Institution’s Innovation Council (IIC) ranking, recognizing its efforts to promote innovation and entrepreneurship among students, faculty, and staff.
The institute has setup the Innovation, Incubation and Entrepreneurship (WCE-IIE) Cell during the academic year 2015-16 with the following objectives:
To foster awareness of innovation, incubation, and entrepreneurship among WCE students and faculty.
To provide a platform for transforming ideas and projects into developed products and commercial ventures.
To offer pre-incubation space for ideation and prototyping.
To nurture pre-incubates in their journey towards establishing startups.
To assist pre-incubates in securing funding and financial support through various government schemes, venture capitalists, investors, and industries.
Activities
Project Contests / Hackathons
Assisting students for participation in innovation / project contests/internships.
Idea Generation and Screening: Organize workshops, ideations, and hackathons to generate and screen innovative ideas through idea validation camps
Mentorship and Guidance: Provide mentorship and guidance to students and faculty to help them develop and refine their innovative ideas.
Prototype Development and Testing: Support students and faculty in developing and testing prototypes of their innovative ideas.
Incubation and Acceleration: Provide incubation and acceleration support to startups and innovative projects, helping them to scale up and commercialize their products or services.
Provide technical and financial support to students and faculty for protecting their intellectual property through IPR processes.
The Innovation Cell at WCE has organized various activities, including workshops, ideations, and hackathons, to generate and screen innovative ideas. The cell has also provided mentorship and guidance to students and faculty to help them develop and refine their innovative ideas. The Innovation Cell at WCE is playing a crucial role in fostering innovation, entrepreneurship, and creativity among students, faculty, and staff, and providing them with opportunities to develop and refine their innovative ideas.
IIE Ranking
The Institution’s Innovation Council (IIC) ranking is a prestigious recognition of an institution’s innovation and entrepreneurial ecosystem. The ranking is based on various parameters, including:
Innovation and Entrepreneurship:
The institution's efforts to promote innovation and entrepreneurship among students, faculty, and staff.
Infrastructure and Resources:
The availability of infrastructure and resources to support innovation and entrepreneurship, such as incubators, accelerators, and funding.
Industry-Academia Collaboration:
The institution's efforts to facilitate collaboration between academia and industry, providing opportunities for students and faculty to work on real-world problems and develop innovative solutions.
Startup Ecosystem:
The institution's efforts to create an entrepreneurial ecosystem that encourages innovation, risk-taking, and experimentation, providing opportunities for students and faculty to develop and scale up their startups.
IIEC team
IIEC is headed by Dr Ajeet Patil. Dr Ajeet is Assistant Professor in Mechanical Engineering with UG and PG from Shivaji University and Ph.D from IIT Roorkee. He is recognized Vibration Analyst Category II, certified by Vibration Institute USA. He has been actively involved in consulting various sugar factories, paper manufacturing units, Kirloskar Pumps, NTPC, ONGC etc. in the field of Vibration measurement and analysis. With an objective to encourage entrepreneurship at WCE, he has been actively coordinating with alumni, investors and industry experts and students. With a vision of making the Entrepreneurship cell at WCE one of the preferable place for innovators to start their entrepreneurial journey, he has been actively involved in setting up the startup ecosystem at WCE.

ICONIC PLACES AT CAMPUS
Dhondumama Sathe Statue
(Shri. Dhondu Krushna Sathe)
The statue of Dhondumama Sathe pays homage to a revered freedom fighter and social reformer. A towering presence on our campus, this statue commemorates the values of courage, resilience, and social responsibility that lie at the heart of Walchand College of Engineering. It stands as a reminder of our commitment to nurturing not just academic excellence but also ethical leadership.
Saraswati Statue
At Walchand College of Engineering, we believe in the holistic development of our students, nurturing their creativity and wisdom. The Saraswati Statue, an embodiment of knowledge and learning, graces our campus with grace and elegance. This statue represents the pursuit of intellectual growth and artistic expression, inspiring students to strive for excellence in all aspects of life.
Founder's Gallery
The Founder’s Gallery is a dedicated space that showcases the life and achievements of our visionary founder, Seth Walchand Hirachand. Through photographs, artifacts, and memorabilia, the gallery offers a glimpse into his remarkable journey and the indelible impact he made on our institution. It serves as a constant source of inspiration for students and reminds us of our rich heritage.
Ganesh Temple
The Ganesh Temple is a spiritual oasis within the campus of Walchand College of Engineering. This ancient temple holds immense significance for the college community, offering a serene space for students, faculty, and visitors to seek solace and spiritual connection. The temple serves as a reminder of the cultural and religious diversity that enriches our campus environment.
The Globe
A notable landmark on our campus, the Globe is a distinctive structure that symbolizes the spirit of exploration and knowledge. Located at a central location, it serves as a meeting point and gathering spot for students. The Globe has become an iconic representation of our commitment to global learning and understanding.
Clock Tower
The Clock Tower stands tall as a timeless symbol of Walchand College of Engineering. This majestic structure not only helps students and faculty keep track of time but also adds a touch of architectural elegance to our campus. The Clock Tower serves as a focal point, standing as a witness to the passage of time and the growth of our institution.
Steam Engine
Nestled within our campus is a captivating piece of engineering history—the Steam Engine. This antique marvel represents the early industrial era and serves as a tribute to the progress of engineering throughout the years. The presence of the Steam Engine on our campus stands as a reminder of the technological advancements that continue to shape our world.
Historic Lecture Halls
Several lecture halls on our campus have witnessed the growth and evolution of Walchand College of Engineering over the years. These halls, with their vintage architecture and classic interiors, provide a unique ambiance for academic discourse and intellectual exchange. Stepping into these spaces is like stepping back in time, inspiring students with a sense of heritage and tradition.

Student Induction Program (SIP) 2024
A comprehensive five-day Student Induction Program (SIP), aligned with AICTE’s holistic development guidelines, was successfully held from 17th to 21st September 2024 on the college campus. The initiative aimed to help students transition smoothly into the academic and cultural environment of professional education by offering structured familiarization and orientation activities.

794 first-year students

Student Life and Extracurricular Activities
:
At Walchand College of Engineering, we believe in holistic development. Our campus offers a vibrant and inclusive student life experience. Numerous clubs, societies, and student organizations cater to diverse interests, including technical, cultural, sports, and community service activities. Students actively participate in events, competitions, and fests, fostering leadership skills, teamwork, and personal growth.
Events that Ignite an Innovative Spark
VISION
A prestigious National Level Technical Symposium under the Shivaji University Lead College Scheme. The event served as a significant platform for budding engineers and tech enthusiasts to showcase their talents and innovative ideas. VISION 2024 featured a range of technical competitions, workshops, and seminars, fostering an environment of learning, collaboration, and cutting-edge technological exploration.
AAKAR
It is a spectacular showcase of innovation and talent. Featuring events like Vectorcad, Hirewave, StructoSticks, Buildcraft, Founder’s Arena, Gatepulse, Yuvasansad, and the flagship event, MiniVerse, Aakar provided students with invaluable skills and experiences. This dynamic lineup emphasized the importance of creativity, technical expertise, and student collaboration, solidifying academic and professional growth.
PRUDENCE
Prudence 2K24, celebrates leadership, teamwork, and continuous learning. The event emphasized holistic development, innovation, and engineering excellence, showcasing the college’s commitment to nurturing well-rounded and innovative engineers.
DSA LAUNCHPAD
This is one of the key events curated to enhance students’ knowledge of Data Structures and Algorithms. The two-day experience included comprehensive sessions, engaging quizzes, and a competitive contest, fostering collaboration among students from various colleges.
ELECTROVERT
Organized by ELESA, it was an exhilarating event that brought together over 1500 participants from more than 10 colleges. This annual gathering featured 10 engaging technical and non-technical sub-events, designed to challenge and inspire participants.
Latest Achievements
WCE SY Btech Students Win Ultimate Roborace
Our SY BTech students emerged 1st prize winners at the Ultimate Roborace Competition at PCCOE, Pune, outshining teams from across Maharashtra in this thrilling. technological challenge.
Smart India Hackathon 2024 Victory
WCE’s team of Shravan Jare, Ranjit Revatkar, Shivam Mathapati, Himanshu Dhage. Gayatri Dabhade, and Rituka Getme won the 1st prize at Smart India Hackathon 2024, receiving Rs. 1 Lakh for their innovative solutions.
Team Aaryans Triumph at BAJA SAEINDIA 2024
Walchand’s Team Aaryans clinched AIR 1 in the Go Green event at BAJA SAEINDIA 2024, excelling in emission control and securing top ranks in Virtual Acceleration, Design, Sales, and CAE categories, showcasing their engineering prowess.

Overview
Overview
Research and consultancy are essential components of an academic institution, as they:
Enhance learning:
Research and consultancy provide opportunities for students to apply theoretical knowledge to real-world problems, developing their critical thinking, problem-solving, and innovation skills.
Foster innovation:
Research and consultancy encourage the development of new ideas, products, and services, driving innovation and entrepreneurship.
Promote knowledge sharing:
Research and consultancy facilitate the sharing of knowledge and expertise between academia, industry, and society, leading to mutual benefits and societal impact.
Generate revenue:
Consultancy and testing services can generate revenue for the institution, supporting its sustainability and growth.
Historical Global Benchmarks
Historically, research and consultancy have played a significant role in the development of many academic institutions. For example:
MIT's Industrial Liaison Program:
Established in 1948, this program facilitated collaboration between MIT researchers and industry partners, driving innovation and economic growth.
Stanford University's Office of Technology Licensing:
Founded in 1970, this office has helped to commercialize Stanford research, leading to the creation of numerous startups and industries.
Research Components
Research in an academic institution can be categorized into several components:
Paper publication:
Publishing research papers in reputable journals and conferences.
Funded projects:
Securing funding for research projects from government agencies, industries, or other organizations.
Student projects:
Guiding students in undergraduate, postgraduate, and Ph.D. research projects.
Centre of Excellence:
Establishing centers of excellence that focus on specific research areas, fostering collaboration and innovation.
Filing Patents:
This is another component of Research recognition
Testing and Consultancy
Testing and consultancy services can be offered to industries and organizations, providing:
Revenue generation:
Generating revenue through testing and consultancy services.
Resource utilization:
Utilizing institutional resources, such as equipment and expertise, for testing and consultancy services.
Knowledge sharing:
Sharing knowledge and expertise with industries and organizations.
Mediums for Research and Development
Mediums for promoting research and consultancy in an academic institution include:
R&D cell:
Establishing a research and development cell to facilitate research activities.
IPR Cell:
Creating an intellectual property rights cell to protect and commercialize research output.
ITC Cell:
Industrial Testing and Consultancy Cell
Measurable Outcomes
Measurable outcomes for research and consultancy in an academic institution include:
Papers and citations:
Tracking the number of research papers published and citations received.
Academic Indices:
Monitoring the institution's ranking in academic indices, such as Scopus or Web of Science and many others
Fund raised:
Tracking the amount of funding secured for research projects.
Projects sanctioned:
Monitoring the number of research projects sanctioned.
Consultancy projects:
Tracking the number of consultancy projects undertaken.
WCE's Research and Consultancy Initiatives
Walchand College of Engineering (WCE) has been actively promoting research and consultancy through:
Establishing research centers:
WCE has established research centers in areas like artificial intelligence, data science, and cybersecurity.
Securing funded projects:
WCE has secured funding for research projects from government agencies and industries.
Encouraging Faculty and student research:
WCE encourages students to undertake research projects, providing guidance and support.
Offering testing and consultancy services:
WCE offers testing and consultancy services to industries and organizations, generating revenue and promoting knowledge sharing.

R&D Cell
R&D Cell
Research and Development Cell acts as nodal agency for all research polices and execution and also facilitation of research.
Dr. A.J. Umbarkar is leading the R&D Cell as Dean R&D
The R&D Cell is responsible for assisting the Academic Council in the performance of the Council’s responsibilities in respect of the establishment and promotion of excellence in the Institute’s research and development, and academic and research training activities. This includes the development, review and monitoring of achievements under the Research & Development,
The Research & Development (R&D) cell serves as the nucleus of innovation, inquiry, and development within our institution. R&D cell acts as nodal agency for all research policies and execution. Established with the vision of fostering a culture of research excellence, the R&D cell aims to encourage faculty, students, researchers and collaborators (industry/academic institutions) to engage in meaningful research that addresses real-world challenges. R&D cell’s mission is to promote interdisciplinary research, facilitate funding opportunities, and support the publication and commercialization of innovative ideas. The R&D cell acts as a bridge between academic knowledge and industry needs, ensuring our research is both relevant and impactful.
Broader key areas of the R&D cell are:
Identifying and promoting research opportunities.
Collaborating with industry and academic institutions.
Supporting funded projects and research proposals.
Organizing seminars, workshops, and conferences.
Assisting in patent filing and intellectual property rights (IPR).
By creating an environment conducive to exploration and experimentation, the R&D cell plays a crucial role in shaping future-ready professionals and contributing to the advancement of science, technology, and society.
Key areas of activities of the R&D cell are:
       The establishment of research and development priorities, and monitoring the quality and quantity of research and development work.
       To improve quality of research, patents, publications, R&D, innovations culture,
       Policies for key areas of activities, creation of ambiance.
       Focus on faculty contribution in R&D, consultancies
       Increasing IPRs from faculty / students.
       To foster the development of multi-disciplinary research endeavors across faculties and departments.
       The protection and commercialization of the IPRs.
       Coordination for getting funds from government departments, industry for R&D projects
       Monitor the application of research funds to ensure that the funds are properly utilized.
       Promote emerging areas of research and development.
  Ensure all facility and expertise is being used for Consultancy and Development
       Improvement in faculty contribution in view of NBA similar parameters and NIRF parameters.
       Increase in professional practices by institution and faculty.
       Consultancy and utilization of human and lab resources
   To formulate incentive schemes for promoting research activities with faculty / students / scholars.
   PG program research focus for projects/dissertation and its quality improvements
       PhD programmes and its policies
       Conferences organization and journals publication
       Quality paper publications
       Joint collaborative work enhancement
       Code of Research Ethics for the responsible practice of research.
    International/National collaboration with Universities/Corporate/Industries by MOUs
       Establishment of Centre of Excellence (COE) in technology domains
       Utilization of Journals and Magazines
       Ph.D. program monitoring

Institute Research Indicators
Institute Research Indicators
Institute Research Indicators are key metrics used to evaluate and monitor the research performance and impact of academic or scientific institutions. These indicators provide quantitative and qualitative insights into an institution’s research activities, productivity, and influence within the scientific community and broader society.
WCE’s research contribution may be seen from Global online platforms
ResearchGate:
WCE researchers have a strong presence on ResearchGate, with over 500 publications, 100 projects, and 150 collaborations showcased on the platform.
IEEE Xplore:
WCE faculty members and students have published over 250 papers in various IEEE conferences and journals, demonstrating their research expertise in electrical engineering, computer science, and other fields.
ScienceDirect:
WCE researchers have published over 110 articles in ScienceDirect journals, covering topics such as materials science, mechanical engineering, and computer science.
ResearcherID:
WCE faculty members have established over 75 ResearcherID profiles, showcasing their publication records and research interests.
ORCID:
Over 200 WCE researchers have created their ORCID profiles, ensuring their research work is easily identifiable and accessible.
Google Scholar:
WCE researchers have a significant presence on Google Scholar, with many faculty members having a high h-index (average h-index: 15), indicating their research impact and citations.
Microsoft Academic:
WCE's research contributions are also visible on Microsoft Academic, which provides a comprehensive overview of the college's research output (over 1,500 publications).
arXiv:
WCE researchers have published over 100 preprints on arXiv, demonstrating their contributions to cutting-edge research in physics, mathematics, and computer science.
DOAJ (Directory of Open Access Journals):
WCE researchers have published over 50 articles in open-access journals listed in DOAJ, promoting the dissemination of knowledge and research findings.
Furter it can be seen through
Publications in Web of Science/Scopus:
WCE researchers have published over 1,000 papers in Web of Science and Scopus-indexed journals, indicating the college's research quality and impact.
Citation Impact:
WCE researchers have received over 10,000 citations for their work, demonstrating the relevance and influence of their research.
IPR/Patent Granted:
WCE faculty members and students have been granted over 50 patents and intellectual property rights, showcasing their innovative research and its potential for real-world applications.
Research Funding:
WCE has secured over ₹ 20 crores cumulatively  in research funding from various government agencies, industries, and organizations, enabling the college to pursue cutting-edge research projects and collaborations.
WCE refers the ScholarGPS, AD scientific indexing and Vidwan.
Common research indicators include the number of publications, citation counts, h-index, research funding acquired, number of patents, collaborations, and participation in national or international projects. Such metrics help institutions assess the effectiveness of their research strategies, benchmark their performance against peers, and inform policy and funding decisions.

Students undertake original research that contributes to the existing body of knowledge.
Advanced Research Methodologies:
Students develop advanced research methodologies, including experimental design, data analysis, and interpretation.
Knowledge Dissemination:
Students disseminate their research findings through publications, presentations, and workshops..
Publications from Students
Students at WCE are encouraged to publish their research findings in reputable journals and conferences. This helps students develop their writing and communication skills, while also contributing to the institution’s research output.
Publication Venues
Reputable Journals:
Students publish their research findings in Scopus-indexed, Web of Science, or UGC-approved journals.
International Conferences:
Students present their research findings at national and international conferences.
Workshops and Seminars:
Students participate in workshops and seminars, presenting their research findings and receiving feedback from experts.

Seth Gulabchand Research Foundation (SGRF)
Seth Gulabchand Research Foundation (SGRF)
Seth Gulabchand Research Foundation (SGRF) was established on the occasion of celebration of silver jubilee of Walchand College of Engineering, Sangli in the year 1973, with major objective of promoting R&D activities at the College. A target of raising corpus of Rs. 10 lakhs was set for the Research Foundation, and use the interest earned on this corpus for application oriented research activities at the college. However till the financial year 1979-80 the College could collect corpus of about Rs. 7.0 lakhs only, out of which Rs. 5.0 lakh was contributed by various companies from the Walchand group.
A Committee drafted Rules and Regulations for working of the SGRF, which were approved by the Administrative Council in its 93rd meeting, held on 29th September 1979 under Item No. 6.
Objectives of SGRF
The Objectives and Activities of the SGRF are to undertake the work of the following nature:
Application oriented research work in the field of Engineering and Technology
Product process development and improvement
Prototype manufacture, testing, and evolution of refined designs
Evolution of special purpose machines, test rigs, processes, etc.
Utilize the proceeds resulting from such work in promoting further research work and development/improvement of the physical facilities at the college
To associate with other Research Institutions or Bodies by way of knowhow sharing in respect of the projects or common interest.
Working of the SGRF
The SGRF activities are supervised through a Research Foundation Committee constituted by the Administrative Council as follows:
Research Foundation Committee has appointed  appoint a Local Advisory Committee (LAC) or an R&D Cell headed by a senior faculty  of WCE, who is coordinating all R&D work under SGRF.
LAC recommends feasibility of the projects proposals under SGRF; suggest ways and means to carry out the R&D work; nominate Principal Investigator/s for the projects; review progress of work and suggest remedial measures. LAC will meet at least 6 times a year and keep minutes of its meeting.
As per the audited balance sheet of SGRF for the financial year 2023-24, the total funds balance is Rs. 127.05 lakh.
Faculty , students are encouraged to undertake eserch projects from these funds and seed funds are provided for this.

ALL INDIA COUNCIL FOR TECHNICAL EDUCATION
NOTIFICATION
New Delhi, the 1st March, 2019
AICTE REGULATIONS ON PAY SCALES, SERVICE CONDITIONS AND MINIMUM
QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE APPOINTMENT OF TEACHERS AND OTHER ACADEMIC STAFF
SUCH AS LIBRARY, PHYSICAL EDUCATION AND TRAINING & PLACEMENT PERSONNEL
IN TECHNICAL INSTITUTIONS AND MEASURES FOR THE MAINTENANCE OF STANDARDS
IN TECHNICAL EDUCATION – (DEGREE) REGULATION, 2019.
F. No. 61-1/RIFD/7th CPC/2016-17.—In exercise of the powers conferred under sub-section (1) of
Section 23 read with Section 10(g), (h) and (i) of the All India Council for Technical Education Act, 1987 (52
of 1987) and after approval of the Government of India vide No. 1 - 37 / 2016 – TS.II, Dated 18th January,
2019 followed by letters of even No. dated 29th January, 2019 and 12th February, 2019, the All India Council
for Technical Education makes the following regulations; namely:
1.0 Short Title, Application and Commencement
1.1 Short Title
These regulations may be called the All India Council for Technical Education Pay Scales, Service
Conditions and Minimum Qualifications for Appointment of Teachers and Other Academic Staff such
as Library, Physical Education and Training & Placement Personnel in Technical Institutions and
Measures for the Maintenance of Standards in Technical Education – (Degree) Regulation, 2019.

1.2 Categories of Institutions to whom the regulations apply
These shall apply to all degree level technical institutions and universities including deemed to be
universities imparting technical education and such other courses / programs approved by AICTE and
areas as notified by the council from time to time.
1.3 Date of Effect
a) Pay Scales and DA: The revised pay-scales shall be effective from 1.1.2016.
b) Other Allowances: Allowances such as Leave Travel Concession, Special Compensatory
Allowances, Children's Education Allowance, Transport Allowance, House Rent Allowance,
Deputation Allowance, House Building Allowance, Travelling Allowance etc. shall be applicable
from the date as notified by the Central Government / respective State and UT Government from
time to time.
1.4 Effective date of application of Service Conditions
a) All other service conditions including Qualifications, Experience, Recruitment, Promotions
publications, training and course requirements etc. shall come into force with effect from the date
of this Gazette Notification.
b) The Qualifications, Experience, Recruitment and Promotions etc. during 01-01-2016 till the issue
of this Gazette Notification shall be governed by All India Council for Technical Education Pay
Scales, Service Conditions and Qualifications for the Teachers and other Academic Staff in
Technical Institutions (Degree) Regulation, 2010 dated 5th March 2010 and subsequent
notifications issued from time to time.
c) Those who are eligible for promotions after the date of publication of this gazette, shall have to
meet the necessary conditions such as additional qualification, undergoing industrial training,
pedagogical training, faculty induction program, publishing research papers etc. However, these
requirements shall be permitted to be fulfilled till 31st July, 2022 so as to enable faculty members
in equipping them for requisite mandatory requirements of this gazette to avail the benefit of
promotion retrospectively from the date of eligibility.
d) For incumbent faculty members, the date of eligibility up to 31st July, 2022 shall be allowed to be
according to the 6th CPC Gazette notification published on 8th November, 2012. All the benefit of
promotion to such candidates be permitted retrospectively on the date when he/she became
eligible.
e) It may be noted that, no further extension would be given beyond 31st July, 2022 and those who
do not meet the essential criteria despite the above grace period, shall lose an opportunity for
getting promotion retrospectively. However, they will be eligible for promotion from the date
they meet these criteria thereafter.
f) In cases, wherein interviews are already conducted either for direct recruitment or for promotions
but candidates did not join, such candidates may be allowed to join. Their further up-gradation
will be governed by this notification.
g) In cases, where advertisement was published, applications invited but interviews have not been
conducted till publication of this notification, the institutes / employers are required to publish
corrigendum and processing of applications must be done in accordance with the provisions
given in this notification.
2.0 General
2.1 Revised Designations and Mode of Appointments
There shall be only three designations in respect of teachers in degree level technical institutions as
far as cadre structure is concerned, namely Assistant Professor, Associate Professor and Professor
as given below in Table 1. Also there shall be no change in the present designations in respect of
Library, Physical Education and Training & Placement Personnel at various levels.
Following mode of appointment shall henceforth be used:

2.2 New Pay Structure
The new pay structure shall involve a pay matrix with an ascending series of levels and ascending
cells in each level. The new pay matrix shall subsume the pay band and grade pay in one simple chart
as given in Annexure - I. The pay matrix shall comprise of two dimensions – a horizontal range of
levels starting from the lowest level in the hierarchy and ascending to the highest level, with the levels
being numbered from 10 to 15 covering the entire gamut of Teachers and other Academic Staff.
Within each level, the salary increases as one goes down vertically, with each progression of going
down represented by a “Cell”. Each Cell within that level represents the steps of annual financial
progression of 3%. On recruitment / promotion, an employee shall join at a particular level and
progress within the level as per the vertical range. The movement shall be based on annual
increments till the time of his /her next promotion. When the employee will receive a promotion,
he/she will progress to the next level in the horizontal range till it exhausts.
2.3 Levels and Cells
The method followed by the 7th CPC shall be adopted in the academic pay structure also, moving
from the concept of Pay Band and Academic Grade Pay to that of Levels and Cells. The changes will
appear only due to the existing difference between the two streams in terms of Academic Grade Pay
vis-à-vis the corresponding Grade Pay. The levels for academic pay shall be numbered as per the
corresponding non-academic level. Thus, the levels are numbered as 10, 11, 12, 13A1, 14, & 15
corresponding to the present AGP of Rs. 6000, 7000, 8000, 9000, 10000 and 12000 respectively.
2.4 Pay Matrix and Fixation of Revised Pay
For Fixation of pay of an Employee in the Pay Matrix as on 1st January 2016, the existing pay (Pay in
Pay Band plus Academic Grade Pay) in the pre-revised structure as on 31st December, 2015 shall be
multiplied by a factor of 2.57, rounded off to the nearest Rupee, and the figure so arrived at, will be
located in that level in the Pay Matrix and if such an identical figure corresponds to any cell in the
applicable level of the Pay Matrix, the same shall be the pay, and if no such cell is available in the
applicable level, the pay shall be fixed at the immediate next higher cell in that applicable level of the
Pay Matrix. If the figure arrived at in this manner is less than the first cell in that level, then the pay
shall be fixed at the first cell of that level of Pay Matrix.
If more than two stages are bunched together, one additional increment equal to 3% may be given for
every two stages bunched, and pay fixed in the subsequent cell in the pay matrix.

2.6 Entry Pay
