B.Tech Curriculum with Minors
B. Tech Curriculum with Minors
Program Educational Objectives (PEOs):
Graduates of Mechanical Engineering programme after a span of three to four years of their graduation will:
PEO1 :
Demonstrate technical competency by applying knowledge to solve problems related to engineering issues.
PEO2 :
Exhibit skills and appropriate attitude to succeed in their professional career.
PEO3 :
Display thirst for emerging technologies and quest for innovation with concern to society and environment.
Programme Outcomes (POs):
The students after successfully completing this programme will have an ability to:
PO 1. Engineering knowledge :
Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems.
PO 2.
Problem analysis :
Identify, formulate, review research literature, and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences.
PO 3. Problem analysis :
Identify, formulate, review research literature, and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences.
PO 4. Conduct investigations of complex problems :
Use research-based knowledge and research methods including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of the information to provide valid conclusions.
PO 5. Modern tool usage :
Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools including prediction and modeling to complex engineering activities with an understanding of the limitations.
PO 6. The engineer and society :
Apply reasoning informed by the contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to the professional engineering practice.
PO 7. Environment and sustainability :
Understand the impact of the professional engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts, and demonstrate the knowledge of, and need for sustainable development.
PO 8. Ethics :
Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities and norms of the engineering practice.
PO 9. Individual and team work :
Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams, and in multidisciplinary settings.
PO 10. Communication :
Communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the engineering community and with society at large, such as, being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations, and give and receive clear instructions.
PO 11. Project management and finance :
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the engineering and management principles and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team, to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.
PO 12. Life-long learning :
Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change.
Program Specific Outcomes (PSO’s):
PSO-1 :
Students will develop an ability to successfully apply the design, thermal and manufacturing principles to analyze and interpret the problems of mechanical engineering or interdisciplinary nature in real time situations and provide analytical and/or software solutions for their overall development.
PSO-2 :
Students will be able to impart technological inputs and acquire managerial skills to become technocrats and entrepreneurs to build the nation, by developing new concepts in emerging fields through intellectual property rights, tech startups and pursuing higher education.
Outcome-Based Educational Philosophy – Mechanical Engineering
Outcome-Based Education (OBE)
is a student-centric educational approach that emphasizes the achievement of clearly defined learning outcomes. For a
B.Tech in Mechanical Engineering
, the OBE philosophy supports the program’s mission to nurture competent mechanical engineers equipped to address real-world challenges through design, analysis, and application of mechanical systems and emerging technologies.
1. Focus on Graduate Attributes:
OBE promotes the development of essential graduate attributes such as:
Analytical and problem-solving skills
Design and innovation thinking
Teamwork and leadership
Effective communication
Ethical and environmental responsibility
These attributes are crucial for mechanical engineers working in interdisciplinary and industrial environments.
2. Student-Centered Learning:
The teaching-learning process is designed to address the diverse learning styles, backgrounds, and professional aspirations of students. This ensures that all learners achieve the intended outcomes through active and personalized learning experiences.
3. Clear Definition of Learning Outcomes:
Learning outcomes are structured across three levels:
Program Outcomes (POs):
Broad competencies such as thermodynamics understanding, mechanical design, project management, and professional ethics.
Program Specific Outcomes (PSOs):
Domain-specific capabilities such as CAD/CAM proficiency, manufacturing process expertise, thermal system analysis, and use of modern engineering tools.
Course Outcomes (COs):
Detailed outcomes at the course level (e.g., the ability to apply heat transfer principles to solve industrial problems).
4. Alignment Across Levels:
The mechanical engineering curriculum, pedagogy, and evaluation strategies are consistently aligned to achieve the defined COs, PSOs, and POs. Teaching methods such as simulations, labs, case studies, and design projects are used to ensure meaningful learning.
5. Continuous Assessment and Feedback:
OBE involves regular monitoring of student progress using rubrics, performance metrics, peer assessments, and industry feedback. This promotes timely identification of gaps and enables continuous curriculum and instruction improvement.
6. Preparation for Lifelong Learning:
Students are trained to embrace lifelong learning through independent projects, MOOCs, internships, and interdisciplinary work. This ensures they stay updated with advancements in areas such as automation, sustainability, materials engineering, and Industry 4.0.

M.Tech Specialisations and Curriculum
M.Tech Specialisations and Curriculum
Specialisations:
Design Engineering, Thermal Engineering and Manufacturing Engineering
M. Tech. Design Engineering
Program Educational Objectives (PEOs):
Post Graduates of Mechanical-Design Engineering program will
PEO1:
Demonstrate the domain expertise and leadership qualities with professional skills to analyze synthesize and execute real life projects in Mechanical-Design engineering and allied fields.
PEO2:
Contribute to the development of scientific/ technological knowledge / innovation in various domains of Mechanical-Design engineering individually, reflectively and/or in team with the aid of modern tools.
PEO3:
Exhibit ethical and social responsibility with concern for diverse local and global Issues.
Programme Outcomes (PO’s):
PO1:
Apply appropriate research methodologies and demonstrate higher order skill individually, in groups to the development works in the domain of Mechanical Design Engineering to solve practical problems. (Research Skill)
PO2:
Communicate with engineering community and society at large, confidently and effectively, through technical report, documentation and presentation, by adhering to appropriate standards. (Communication)
PO3:
Demonstrate degree of mastery in Mechanical Design Engineering at a level higher than the requirements in the appropriate bachelor program. (Scholarship of Knowledge)
PO4:
Apply appropriate research methodologies to develop scientific and technical knowledge to understand group dynamics, which will lead towards collaborative multidisciplinary research. (Critical Thinking and Problem Solving)
PO5:
Analyze complex problems optimally in Mechanical-Design Engineering for real life solutions and further to solve them by considering various aspects like, life- long learning, self-motivation, socio-economics, ethical behaviour. (Ethical Practices, Social responsibility and Life-long learning)
PO6:
Acquire expertise in latest trends and technologies in the fields of Mechanical- Design Engineering like, Stress analysis, Vibration analysis, Condition monitoring, Noise Control and contribute to innovation. (Programme specific outcome)
M. Tech Thermal Engineering
Program Educational Objectives (PEOs):
Post Graduates of Thermal Engineering program will
PEO1:
Demonstrate the domain expertise and leadership qualities with professional skills to analyze, synthesize and execute real life projects in Thermal Engineering and allied fields.
PEO2:
Contribute to the development of scientific / technological knowledge / innovation in various domains of Thermal Engineering individually, reflectively and / or in team with the aid of modern tools.
PEO3:
Exhibit ethical and social responsibility with concern for diverse local and global issues.
Programme Outcomes (PO’s)
:
PO1:
Apply appropriate research methodologies and demonstrate higher order skill individually, in groups to the development works in the domain of Thermal Engineering to solve practical problems. (Research Skill)
PO2:
Communicate with engineering community and society at large, confidently and effectively, through technical report, documentation and presentation, by adhering to appropriate standards. (Communication)
PO3
: Demonstrate degree of mastery Thermal Engineering at a level higher than the requirements in the appropriate bachelor program. (Scholarship of Knowledge)
PO4:
Apply appropriate research methodologies to develop scientific and technical knowledge to understand group dynamics, which will lead towards collaborative multidisciplinary research. (Critical Thinking and Problem Solving)
PO5:
Analyze complex problems optimally in Thermal Engineering for real life solutions and further to solve them by considering various aspects like, life-long learning, self-motivation, socio-economics, ethical behaviour. (Ethical Practices, Social responsibility and Life-long learning)
PO6:
Gain expertise in latest trends and technologies in the fields of Thermal Engineering like, computational, mathematical, Modelling software and apply them efficiently to carry out project independently. (Programme specific outcome)
M. Tech Manufacturing Engineering
Program Educational Objectives (PEOs):
Post Graduates of Manufacturing Engineering program will
PEO1:
Demonstrate the domain expertise and leadership qualities with professional skills to analyze, synthesize and execute real life projects in Manufacturing Engineering and allied fields.
PEO2:
Contribute to the development of scientific/technological knowledge/innovation in various domains of Manufacturing Engineering individually, reflectively and/or in team with the aid of modern tools.
PEO3:
Exhibit ethical and social responsibility with concern for diverse local and global issues.
Programme Outcomes (PO’s):
PO1:
Apply appropriate research methodologies and demonstrate higher order skill individually, in groups to the development works in the domain of Manufacturing Engineering to solve practical problems. (Research Skill)
PO2:
Communicate with engineering community and society at large, confidently and effectively, through technical report, documentation and presentation, by adhering to appropriate standards. (Communication)
PO3:
Demonstrate degree of mastery in Manufacturing Engineering at a level higher than the requirements in the appropriate bachelor program. (Scholarship of Knowledge)
PO4:
Apply appropriate research methodologies to develop scientific and technical knowledge to understand group dynamics, which will lead towards collaborative multidisciplinary research. (Critical Thinking and Problem Solving)
PO5:
Analyze complex problems optimally in Manufacturing Engineering for real life solutions and further to solve them by considering various aspects like, life-long learning, self-motivation, socio-economics, ethical behaviour. (Ethical Practices, Social responsibility and Life-long learning)
PO6:
Gain expertise in latest trends and technologies in the fields of Manufacturing Engineering like, manufacturing processes, automation, robotics, mechatronics, advanced welding, Industrial engineering and operations research, FEM, etc. and apply them efficiently to carry out project independently. (Programme specific outcome)

Academic Planning & Activities
Academic Planning & Activities
The Mechanical Engineering Department is committed to fostering academic excellence through innovative, interdisciplinary, and student-focused strategies. These practices are structured to ensure holistic development, practical skills, and industry readiness among students.
1. Curriculum Design and Development
Interdisciplinary Integration:
Courses on cutting-edge technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things (IoT), and Sustainable Engineering are integrated into the curriculum.
Industry-Aligned Revisions:
The curriculum is regularly updated to align with industry trends and national accreditation guidelines (NBA, NAAC).
Experiential Learning:
Inclusion of project-based learning modules, design thinking, and hands-on activities to encourage problem-solving and application-oriented learning.
2. Research and Innovation Initiatives
Focused Research Groups:
Active groups in emerging domains like Robotics, Machine Learning, Renewable Energy, and Advanced Manufacturing.
Industry Collaboration:
Joint research initiatives, funded projects, and industrial internships to promote real-world problem-solving.
Innovation Events:
Organization of ideation contests, hackathons, and technical challenges to stimulate creativity and innovation.
3. Laboratory and Infrastructure Development
Advanced Lab Facilities:
Upgraded laboratories equipped with CNC machines, 3D printers.
Centres of Excellence:
Specialized centers in Robotics, Refrigeration, Mechatronics, to facilitate in-depth research and skill development.
4. Comprehensive Mentorship Program
Personalized Mentoring:
Each student is assigned a faculty mentor to guide academic, personal, and career development.
Consistent Monitoring:
Regular one-on-one meetings to assess progress and address challenges.
5. Class Advisors
Holistic Monitoring:
Class teachers oversee academic performance, attendance, and student well-being.
Goal Setting:
Support students in setting academic and professional goals through structured interactions.
6. Departmental Committees
Board of Studies (BoS):
Reviews and approves curriculum, integrates industry skills, and oversees accreditation readiness.
Department Advisory Board (DAB):
Guides long-term planning and academic excellence.
PhD Progress Committee:
Monitors research progress and ensures quality outcomes for doctoral scholars.
7. Experiential Learning Emphasis
Project-Based Learning:
Integration of hands-on projects across semesters to enhance critical thinking.
Industry-Linked Learning:
Live projects, guest lectures, and workshops from industry professionals.
Digital Tools:
Use of simulation platforms, CAD software, and coding environments.
8. Projects and Mini-Projects
Progressive Project Work:
Mini-projects in 5th and 6th semesters, major projects in the final year focused on real-world challenges.
Innovative Themes:
Topics include Smart Manufacturing, Green Energy Systems, and Industrial Automation.
Showcases and Hackathons:
Project exhibitions and competitions to encourage innovation and teamwork.
9. Industry Visits and Internships
Real-World Exposure:
Visits to manufacturing plants, R&D centers, and start-ups.
Internship Programs:
Mandatory internships during semester breaks provide practical experience.
Recent Visit Example:
In A.Y. 2024–25, students visited to Cooper Corporation Satara, Swabhimani Dairy.
10. Seminars, Workshops, and Technical Events
Expert Lectures:
Sessions on advanced topics such as Smart Materials, Fluid Simulation, and Automation.
Skill-Building Workshops:
Training on tools like MATLAB, ANSYS, Python, and SolidWorks.
Technical Competitions:
Regular hackathons, design challenges, and poster presentations.
11. Skill Development Initiatives
.
Soft Skills Training:
Communication, team collaboration, leadership, and interview preparation.
12. Research-Oriented Activities
Student Research Groups:
Encouragement to explore areas like Thermodynamics, IoT in Manufacturing
Publications and Conferences:
Support for publishing papers, attending conferences, and securing innovation funding.
13. Technical Clubs and Extracurricular Activities
Active Clubs:
Student-led clubs including Robotics Club, Auto Club, and Innovation Cell to promote peer learning.
Competitions and Networking:
Intra- and inter-institutional events to foster collaboration and competitive spirit.
Holistic Development:
Focus on both technical and non-technical growth through active participation.
14. Continuous Evaluation and Improvement
Ongoing Feedback Mechanisms:
Regular collection of student and faculty feedback for pedagogical improvements.
Assessment Structure:
Theory:
In-Semester Evaluation 1 & 2 (20 Marks), Mid-Semester (30 Marks), End-Semester (50 Marks).
Laboratory:
Continuous Assessments (30 Marks), Final Exam (40 Marks).
Flexible Evaluation Modes:
Includes oral tests, presentations, quizzes, and MCQs.
15. Effective Program Delivery
Modern Pedagogy:
Use of smart boards, interactive lectures, and digital simulations.
E-Learning Integration:
Virtual labs, MOOCs, and blended learning tools.
Faculty Innovations:
Engaging teaching strategies including flipped classrooms, video lectures, and collaborative projects.
16. Industry-Academia Collaboration
Internships and Co-op Programs:
Strong industry linkage for student placements and real-time learning.
Startup Ecosystem:
Incubation support for student-led innovations and product development.
Curriculum Input:
Regular consultation with industry experts for relevant skill inclusion and mentorship. This comprehensive approach ensures Mechanical Engineering graduates are not only academically proficient but also well-prepared for dynamic industry roles and future research opportunities

Students Development
Students Development
To enhance technical exposure and professional development, the department actively supports student chapters of leading professional bodies such as ASME, SAE, ASHRAE, and ISHRAE. Through these chapters, a variety of workshops, seminars, and hands-on activities are conducted regularly.
Our students enthusiastically participate in prestigious national and state-level competitions such as M-BAJA, E-BAJA, Efficycle, SUPRA, ACREX, and Go-Kart, showcasing their creativity, teamwork, and technical prowess.
In addition, students of the department have formed the Mechanical Engineering Students Association (MESA), which plays a key role in organizing a variety of co-curricular and extracurricular events. These include weekly club sessions, aptitude tests, and guest seminars by eminent professionals from industry and academia. Every year, MESA organizes a state-level technical symposium called VERTEX, which brings together students from across the region to participate in a range of competitive and knowledge-sharing events. VERTEX aims at the holistic development of students by nurturing their technical skills, leadership qualities, teamwork, and social responsibility.
The department has successfully implemented a scheme under the Technology Information, Forecasting and Assessment Council (TIFAC), which has significantly enhanced industry-academia collaboration. Through this initiative, students and faculty members actively engage with technologically deficient Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), providing them with valuable technical support and consultancy. This real-world exposure enriches the students’ practical understanding while contributing to the growth and modernization of local industries.
In addition to TIFAC, the department is also supported by the Rajiv Gandhi Science and Technology Commission (RGSTC), Government of Maharashtra. This scheme aims to promote applied research, innovation, and technological development in higher education institutions. Through RGSTC funding, the department is able to undertake impactful research projects strengthen linkages with industry and society.
Together, these schemes have played a pivotal role in fostering practical learning, research-driven innovation, and technology transfer, making the department a key contributor to the region’s technological advancement.
Internship from reputed industries such as DRDO, Dassault Systems, Cummins, HAL, John Deere, Blue Star, Siemens, Atlas Copco, Thermax etc. are offered to the postgraduate students. So student can join these companies and complete his/her dissertation work at respective industry.
Our students have been consistently placed in a wide range of reputed core and software companies, reflecting the department’s strong focus on technical excellence and industry readiness. In the core engineering and manufacturing sector, students have secured positions in leading organizations such as Tata Motors, John Deere, Atlas Copco, Mahindra & Mahindra, Eaton India, L&T, Dassault Systèmes, Toyo Engineering, Fiat India, Man Truck, Siemens Energy, Faurecia Forvia, Burns & McDonnell, Cooper Lighting Solutions, Philips, Hindustan Unilever Limited, Schneider Electric, and KSB Pumps.
In the software and IT domain, our graduates have also been successfully placed in top companies including Infosys, TCS, Cognizant, and Siemens. Demonstrating the strength of our training and industry connections, the department achieved a remarkable 100% placement of eligible students in the academic year 2024-25. This diverse placement profile highlights the multi-disciplinary skills and adaptability of our students and underscores the department’s commitment to preparing graduates for both core industry roles and technology-driven careers.
Our students actively prepare for competitive exams such as GATE, GRE, TOEFL and CAT, with many securing admissions to prestigious institutions like the IITs, NITs, and IIMs, as well as top universities abroad in countries like the United States, Germany, and Australia. Students are actively involved in MPSC/UPSC preparations and achievements. We take immense pride in our alumni, several of whom have risen to hold senior leadership and executive roles in renowned organizations including ISRO, DRDO, Tata Motors, Bell Telecom, L&T, 3D PLM, HAL, Hero MotoCorp, Siemens, Mercedes, Infosys, Wipro, and other prominent manufacturing and service companies.
In summary, the department is committed to fostering holistic development in students by encouraging active participation in both academic and extracurricular activities. Our goal is to equip students with the knowledge, skills, and leadership qualities necessary to excel as engineers, entrepreneurs, and professionals who contribute meaningfully to society. We strive to provide quality education that blends solid theoretical foundations with practical experience, enabling our graduates to meet the dynamic challenges of the industry and making Mechanical Engineering a preferred choice among aspiring students.

Arranged seminar on, “ISHRAE Membership Promotion” for T.Y. B. Tech Students
The “ISHRAE Membership Promotion” seminar was organized for the T.Y. B.Tech students to enlighten them about the benefits and importance of becoming a member of the Indian Society of Heating, Refrigerating, and Air Conditioning Engineers (ISHRAE). The seminar aimed to provide an understanding of the resources, career opportunities, and professional growth ISHRAE offers to students pursuing engineering in the HVAC&R (Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning, and Refrigeration) field.
The seminar covered the following key points:
Introduction to ISHRAE: An overview of the society’s mission, its role in the HVAC&R industry, and how it serves as a platform for learning and networking.
Benefits of ISHRAE Membership: Insights into the numerous advantages, including access to industry events, technical resources, publications, seminars, and workshops, which can significantly enhance students’ skills and knowledge.
Career Opportunities: Information about how ISHRAE membership opens doors to internships, mentorships, and job opportunities, helping students build strong professional networks.
Technical and Professional Development: A discussion on how being a part of ISHRAE helps in skill-building, certifications, and keeping up with the latest industry trends and innovations in HVAC&R.
Interactive Session: An engaging Q&A session where students could ask questions and get detailed responses about how to utilize ISHRAE’s offerings to their advantage.

ASME Student Chapter: Support to design and locations of value education infrastructure.
The ASME (American Society of Mechanical Engineers) Student Chapter plays a pivotal role in shaping the next generation of engineers by offering support in the design and development of educational infrastructure that fosters both technical and value-based learning. This initiative involves designing spaces that integrate both engineering principles and values education, preparing students for their professional careers in a holistic manner.
The support provided by the ASME Student Chapter can be outlined in the following key areas:
Designing Collaborative Spaces: ASME provides guidance in creating spaces that encourage interaction, brainstorming, and collaboration. These spaces are designed to accommodate group discussions, workshops, and projects, aligning with modern educational techniques that emphasize teamwork and real-world problem solving.
Integration of Value-Based Learning: ASME assists in the creation of learning environments that not only focus on technical knowledge but also emphasize the importance of ethical practices, sustainability, and social responsibility in engineering. This is critical in shaping engineers who are mindful of the societal and environmental impacts of their work.

The inauguration of the ISHRAE (Indian Society of Heating, Refrigerating, and Air Conditioning Engineers) chapter was a momentous occasion, marking the beginning of a new chapter for the students in the field of HVAC&R. The event was attended by faculty members, industry professionals, and enthusiastic students eager to explore the world of heating, ventilation, air conditioning, and refrigeration. The inauguration featured a brief overview of ISHRAE’s goals, benefits of membership, and its impact on students’ professional development. It set the stage for exciting learning opportunities, workshops, and technical events aimed at bridging the gap between academic knowledge and industry practices. Volunteers enthusiastically took part in the cleaning process, while also raising awareness about the importance of maintaining a clean environment. Through this initiative, the participants not only contributed to improving their surroundings but also reinforced the values of discipline, responsibility, and social service, in line with Mahatma Gandhi’s vision of a cleaner, healthier nation.

On 27th September 2024, an industrial visit was organized to Cooper Corporation, Satara, offering students a valuable opportunity to explore the operations of one of India’s leading manufacturers of high-performance engines and components. B.Tech Curriculum with Minors
Curriculum
– The B. Tech curriculum in electrical engineering is designed to provide students with a comprehensive education in electrical engineering.
Curriculum
– The B. Tech curriculum in electrical engineering is designed to provide students with a comprehensive education in electrical engineering. In the Academic Year 2024-2025 curriculum of First year and Second Year is implemented as per NEP 2020 policy which includes multidisciplinary minor (MDM) as well. CSE department offers MDM in electrical engineering.
Minors
Program Objective and Outcome
Graduates of UG Programme after completing their graduation in Electrical Engineering will be able to:
PEO1:
Pursue successful career in diversified sector like industry, government organisations, entrepreneurship and / or higher education in Electrical.
PEO2:
Contribute as active members of the society as an individual or in a team to analyse, design and implement solutions to solve real life problems with due concern for the environment.
PEO3:
Exhibit leadership skills, effective communication skill and life-long learning needed to succeed in a multidisciplinary environment with commitment to ethical standard.
Program Outcomes
PO1: Engineering Knowledge:
Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems.
PO2: Problem Analysis:
Identify, formulate, review research literature, and Analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences.
PO3:  Design/Development of Solutions:
Design solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for the public health and safety, and the cultural, societal, and environmental considerations.
PO4: Conduct Investigations of Complex Problems:
Use research-based knowledge and research methods including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of the information to provide valid conclusions.
PO5: Modern Tool Usage:
Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools including prediction and modelling to complex engineering activities with an understanding of the limitations.
PO6: The Engineer and Society:
Apply reasoning informed by the contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to the professional engineering practice
PO7: Environment and Sustainability:
Understand the impact of the professional engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts, and demonstrate the knowledge of, and need for sustainable development.
PO8: Ethics:
Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities and norms of the engineering practice.
PO9: Individual and Team Work:
Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams, and in multidisciplinary settings.
PO10: Communication:
Communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the engineering community and with society at large, such as, being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations, and give and receive clear instructions.
PO11: Project Management and Finance:
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the engineering and management principles and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team, to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.
PO12: Life-long learning:
Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change.
Program Specific Outcomes
PSO1:
Critically understand and apply the concepts of generation, transmission and distribution for Electrical Power System Operation, Control and Protection.
PSO2:
Software System Design: Gain in-depth knowledge and use advanced techniques to operate/ control electrical machine/ drives used in various industries.
Outcome Based Educational Philosophy
Outcome-Based Education (OBE) focuses on achieving specific outcomes in terms of knowledge, skills, and attitudes that students are expected to demonstrate upon graduation. For a B. Tech in Electrical Engineering, the OBE philosophy aligns with the program’s mission to develop competent engineers capable of solving real-world problems using modern technologies.
Focus on Graduate Attributes:
OBE emphasizes the development of key attributes such as problem-solving, critical thinking, teamwork, and effective communication, which are essential for computer engineers.
Student-Centered Learning:
The learning process is tailored to meet the needs and aspirations of the students, ensuring that each learner achieves predefined outcomes.
Clear Definition of Learning Outcomes:
Learning outcomes are categorized into Program Outcomes (POs), Program Specific Outcomes (PSOs), and Course Outcomes (COs):
POs:
Define general competencies (e.g., problem analysis, ethical responsibility).
PSOs:
Focus on domain-specific skills (e.g., Electrical Power System and Machines and Drives).
COs:
Specify what students will achieve in individual courses.
Alignment across Levels:
The curriculum, teaching methodologies, and assessment strategies are aligned with achieving the defined outcomes.
Continuous Assessment and Feedback:
The OBE framework uses tools like rubrics, surveys, and assessments to measure outcomes and provide feedback for continuous improvement.
Preparation for Lifelong Learning:
Encourages adaptability and lifelong learning to remain relevant in a rapidly evolving field like Electrical Engineering.

The M.Tech in Power System Engineering and Control and Instrumentation Engineering at Walchand College of Engineering (WCE) focuses on advanced computational theories, cutting-edge technologies, and research. It blends rigorous coursework with hands-on projects, covering areas like power system protection, stability, and adaptive control system, process instrumentation preparing students for careers in academia, research, and industry.
Curriculum:
The M.Tech curriculum is designed to provide students with advanced knowledge and skills in their chosen specialisation. The curriculum is designed to provide students with a comprehensive education in Electrical power system & control system engineering. Academic Planning & Activities
Academic Planning & Activities
The Electrical Engineering Department implements several innovative and student-centric practices to ensure a well-rounded academic experience. These include:
Curriculum Design and Development
Integration of interdisciplinary courses (e.g., Electric Vehicle Technology).
Regular curriculum revisions to align with industry trends and accreditation guidelines (e.g. NBA, NAAC).
Inclusion of project-based and experiential learning modules.
Research and Innovation Initiatives
Establishing research groups for emerging fields like Smart Grid, Electric Vehicle, Energy storage systems and Sustainable Engineering.
Collaboration with industry for funded research projects and internships.
Laboratory and Infrastructure Development
Upgrading labs with advanced tools like PLC equipment lab, lab set up with MATLAB, ETAP and Mi-POWER software.
Promoting virtual labs and remote experimentation for online learners.
Comprehensive Mentorship Program
Each student is assigned a faculty mentor to provide personalized guidance in academics, career planning, and personal development.
Regular mentorship meetings ensure continuous tracking of student progress and timely intervention for challenges.
1:20 ratio is maintained while assigning faculty to each student batch.

Every class has a designated class teacher who monitors academic performance, attendance, and overall well-being.
Class Teachers collaborate with students to set academic and career goals while ensuring compliance with institutional requirements.

Departmental faculty use different innovative methods to engage lecturers like video lecture, interactive lectures, Discussions etc.

Partnerships for internships, co-op programs, and guest lectures.
Establishing incubation centres for student start-ups.
Inviting industry experts for curriculum input and mentorship.

ESSA:
Electrical Engineering Students’ Association (EESA) is a student organization pioneered in technical activities, founded by U. Gudaru. It is the first and foremost established club at WCE, Sangli. It is active since 1976, with the concept of the founder, guidance of staff advisor, an executive row of third year students with the guidance of final year students and
Full-fledged support of first year and second year students together enhances the power of
EESA.
EESA conducts various activities throughout the year to help students in increasing their technical knowledge and soft skills. EESA helps students pursue their technical interests thereby increasing their engineering expertise along with imparting skills.
Since its inception, EESA is striving hard to meet its motto “To enhance technical comprehension, soft skills and managerial dexterity” of students pursuing electrical engineering in Walchand College of Engineering, Sangli.
TECHNOCRAT is a state level technical symposium arranged by Electrical Engineering Students’ Association (EESA). This event is organized each year with the focus to give students irrespective of their departments and colleges a biased platform to showcase their skills and a chance to share their ideas in such a state level summit. Events are designed in such a way that their technical knowledge will be helpful to apply this knowledge in practical life.
TECHNOCRAT has been surpassing its previous benchmarks in terms of no of participants participating in it along with the quality of events EESA delivering it. It facilitates sharing of knowledge and new technologies with different entrepreneurs, professors, researchers, and students. This facilitates to improve the competitive spirit of students and helps them to develop with the constantly moving world. This is the sole purpose of organizing TECHNOCRAT.

B.Tech Electronics Engineering Curriculum
B.Tech Electronics Engineering Curriculum
Curriculum:
The B.Tech curriculum in Electronics Engineering is designed to provide students with a comprehensive education in Electronics related courses. In the Academic Year 2024-2025 curriculum of First year and Second Year is implemented as per NEP 2020 policy which includes multidisciplinary minor (MDM) as well. Electronics department offers MDM in Electronics and (14 credits).
Outcome-Based Educational Philosophy in Electronics Engineering
Focus on Learning Outcomes:
Program Outcomes (POs):
Broad skills and knowledge students should have after graduation (e.g., problem-solving, design skills, ethics).
Program Specific Outcomes (PSOs):
Competencies specific to Electronics Engineering (e.g., circuit analysis, embedded system design).
Course Outcomes (COs):
What students are expected to learn at the end of each course.
Backward Curriculum Design:
Starts with defining desired graduate attributes and outcomes, and then designs the curriculum, teaching methods, and assessments to meet these goals.
Continuous Assessment & Feedback:
Direct Assessments:
Assignments, lab work, exams mapped to COs and POs.
Indirect Assessments:
Surveys, feedback from students, alumni, and employers.
Regular monitoring ensures course and program improvements.
Industry-Relevant Skills:
Electronics Engineering under OBE emphasizes:
Hands-on design and simulation (e.g., using tools like MATLAB, PSPICE)
Industry projects and internships
Skills in VLSI, IoT, Embedded Systems, and Communication technologies
Lifelong Learning & Ethics:
Encourages self-learning, innovation, and ethical responsibility.
Integrates modern tools and interdisciplinary knowledge.
Student-Centric Learning:
Promotes active learning, peer collaboration, and problem-solving.
Encourages participation in mini-projects, hackathons, and design challenges.

Academic Planning and Activities
Curriculum Design and Development
Integration of interdisciplinary courses

Research and Innovation Initiatives

Collaboration with industry for funded research projects and internships.
Organizing hackathons, ideation contests, and innovation challenges.
Laboratory and Infrastructure Development
Upgrading labs with advanced tools like Cadence, NetSim
Setting up centers of excellence for specialized fields like Embedded System, VLSI and IoT
Promoting virtual labs and remote experimentation for online learners.
Comprehensive Mentorship Program
Each student is assigned a faculty mentor to provide personalized guidance in academics, career planning, and personal development.
Regular mentorship meetings ensure continuous tracking of student progress and timely intervention for challenges.
1:15 ratio is maintained while assigning faculty to each student batch.

Every class has a designated class teacher who monitors academic performance, attendance, and overall well-being.
Class Teachers collaborate with students to set academic and career goals while ensuring compliance with institutional requirements.

Departmental Committees
Board of Studies (BoS)
: The BoS is the primary academic advisory committee of a department in an educational institution. It is responsible for designing, reviewing, and updating the curriculum and syllabus for various courses to keep pace with academic and industry developments. It ensures academic standards and the relevance of teaching, learning, and evaluation processes. Typically includes departmental faculty, subject experts from academia and industry, and sometimes alumni and student representatives. It makes recommendations on teaching methods, reference materials, and academic infrastructure. Usually meets once or twice a year or as needed to revise or develop academic policies and programs. Its suggestions are forwarded to the Academic Council for final approval and implementation.
Department Advisory Board (DAB)”
The DAB provides strategic guidance to the department for its long-term growth and alignment with industry and societal needs. It typically includes senior faculty members, industry experts, alumni, and sometimes representatives from academia, research organizations, and regulatory bodies. It periodically reviews and advises on the department’s vision, mission, Program Educational Objectives (PEOs), and outcomes. Offers input on curriculum development to ensure alignment with current industry practices and future trends. It acts as a platform to incorporate feedback from stakeholders like employers, alumni, and professional bodies into academic planning. Suggests measures to enhance students’ industry-readiness, soft skills, and employability. It plays a crucial role in supporting the department for accreditations like NBA by reviewing and validating PEOs, PSOs, and outcome attainment.
The
PhD Progress and Evaluation Committee
is responsible for monitoring and guiding the progress of research scholars to ensure the quality and timely completion of research work.
Program Delivery with Emphasis on Experiential Learning:
Focuses on engaging students actively in the learning process through real-world experiences rather than passive content delivery.
Regular practical labs, simulation-based exercises, and prototyping activities help reinforce theoretical concepts.
Students work on real-time projects, mini-projects, and capstone projects to apply classroom knowledge to solve practical problems.
Projects and Mini-Projects
Students undertake
mini-projects
in fifth and sixth semesters and
major projects
in final year, encouraging application-based learning and research problem statements.
Projects often focus on solving real-world problems, with themes such as Smart Cities, E-Healthcare, and Green Computing.
Organizing project showcases and hackathons to promote innovation and teamwork.
Mini Project and mega project guides are assigned to each group to evaluate student progress.
Industry Visits and Internships
Regular industrial visits to top IT/core companies, startups, and research centers provide students with practical exposure to organizational workflows and cutting-edge technologies.
Internship opportunities during semester breaks enable students to gain hands-on experience in real-world projects and applications.

International Conference
The department organizes conference to enrich the knowledge of students. This provides a platform for both the faculty and students to share their knowledge and to hold discussion with eminent people from both academia and industry and also with their peers. These events help the students to acquire different soft skills.

B Tech Curriculum with Minors
B.Tech Curriculum with Minors
Vision
To produce capable computer science & engineering graduates with an aptitude for research and leadership.
Mission
To promote excellence in CSE education through relevant academic curricula and innovative teaching learning processes.
To offer different opportunities to the students for development of professional skills.
To nurture critical thinking and creativity in the students.
To inculcate in the student’s life-long learning attitude and sensitivity towards society & environment.
Curriculum
The B.Tech curriculum in computer engineering is designed to provide students with a comprehensive education in computer science and engineering. In the Academic Year 2024-2025 curriculum of First year and Second Year is implemented as per NEP 2020 policy which includes multidisciplinary minor (MDM) as well. CSE department has offered MDM in Computer Science and Engineering and FinTech (each of mandatory 14 credits).
Minors
The department offers minors in the emerging area like Blockchain and Security.
Program Educational Objectives (PEOs)
Graduates of UG Programme after completing their graduation in Computer Science and Engineering will be able to
PEO1
Demonstrate technical competency by applying knowledge to solve problems related to engineering issues.
PEO2
Exhibit skills and right attitude to succeed in their professional Career.
PEO3
Display thirst for emerging technologies and quest for innovation with concern to society and environment.
Program Outcomes (POs)
PO1
Engineering Knowledge
: Apply knowledge of mathematics, natural science, computing, engineering fundamentals and an engineering specialization as specified in WK1 to WK4 respectively to develop to the solution of complex engineering problems.
PO2
Problem Analysis
: Identify, formulate, review research literature and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions with consideration for sustainable development. (WK1 to WK4)
PO3
Design/Development of Solutions
: Design creative solutions for complex engineering problems and design/develop systems/components/processes to meet identified needs with consideration for the public health and safety, whole-life cost, net zero carbon, culture, society and environment as required. (WK5)
PO4
Conduct Investigations of Complex Problems
: Conduct investigations of complex engineering problems using research-based knowledge including design of experiments, modeling, analysis & interpretation of data to provide valid conclusions. (WK8)
PO5
Engineering Tool Usage
: Create, select and apply appropriate techniques, resources and modern engineering & IT tools, including prediction and modeling recognizing their limitations to solve complex engineering problems. (WK2 and WK6)
PO6
The Engineer and The World
: Analyze and evaluate societal and environmental aspects while solving complex engineering problems for its impact on sustainability with reference to economy, health, safety, legal framework, culture and environment. (WK1, WK5, and WK7)
PO7
Ethics
: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics, human values, diversity and inclusion; adhere to national & international laws. (WK9)
PO8
Individual and Collaborative Team work
: Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse/multi-disciplinary teams.
PO9
Communication
: Communicate effectively and inclusively within the engineering community and society at large, such as being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations considering cultural, language, and learning differences.
PO10
Project Management and Finance
: Apply knowledge and understanding of engineering management principles and economic decision-making and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team, and to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.
PO11
Life-Long Learning
: Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability for i) Independent and life-long learning ii) adaptability to new and emerging technologies and iii) critical thinking in the broadest context of technological change. (WK8)
Program Specific Outcomes:
PSO1
Apply knowledge of Databases, Networking, Security, Software Engineering, AI and allied domains to design, implement and validate efficient solutions for real world problems.
PSO2
Apply cutting edge technologies to excel in professional career, entrepreneurship, research and higher studies in Computer Science & Engineering Domain.

The M.Tech specialization in Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) focuses on advanced computational theories, cutting-edge technologies, and research. Resources
Resources
Laboratories
The department has all types of modern teaching- learning resources in the department.
The department is equipped with state-of-the-art laboratories, providing students with the necessary resources for practical learning and specialized software tools.
The technical staff is appointed by the institute and allotted by the Head of the department considering their skill set, by issuing formal order letters.
Adequate technical manpower ensures smooth laboratory operations, technical support, and assistance to students and faculty for academic and research activities. The list of laboratories and technical manpower is mentioned in Table
As and when any facility is created at the department in the form of hardware or software, the support staff is given training and certification to ensure their scaling up. Refer image below
Centres
Name of Lab
Details
Networking and IoT Laboratory
The Network and IoT Laboratory is equipped with state-of-the-art infrastructure to support hands-on learning and research in networking and Internet of Things domains. The lab houses 21 high-performance Dell computer systems featuring Intel Core i7 processors, 16 GB RAM, 1 TB HDD, and 256 GB NVMe SSDs, all running on Windows 11 Pro, providing a robust platform for simulation, programming, and system configuration. Networking infrastructure includes two 24-port network switches (Extreme and TRENDnet), enabling practical exposure to LAN setup and network management. Additionally, the lab is supported by a VERTIV UPS with a 1 KVA capacity and 16 Exide SMF batteries to ensure uninterrupted power supply. For IoT development, the lab includes a comprehensive IoT kit comprising Raspberry Pi boards, various sensors, displays, and communication modules, facilitating prototype development and experimentation. The presence of a Samsung digital TV and a Hitachi LCD projector further aids in interactive teaching and demonstrations.
Database Engineering Laboratory
The Database Engineering Laboratory is well-furnished with computing and peripheral infrastructure to support practical learning and project development in the areas of database design, management, and application development. It features 21 Dell computer systems with Intel Core i7-9700 CPUs, 16 GB RAM, 1 TB HDD, and 250 GB NVMe SSDs, delivering a reliable and high-speed computing environment, all running on Windows 11 Pro. An additional Dell system is dedicated for CCTV monitoring, configured with an Intel i7-2600 CPU and 4 GB RAM. For network connectivity, the lab is equipped with a 24+4 port D-Link Gigabit Smart Managed Switch and a 4U D-Link network rack, ensuring stable and scalable networking. The lab also includes a 3 KVA Powergun Alfa Online UPS with 8 Exide SMF batteries to provide uninterrupted power supply. Visualization and presentations are supported by an Epson EB-W49 LCD projector. Printing needs are met through an HP LaserJet 1020 and an Epson All-in-One L565 printer, facilitating documentation and report generation. This comprehensive setup supports a robust environment for conducting database-centric coursework, research, and development activities.
Image Processing and Computer Vision Laboratory
The Image Processing and Computer Vision Laboratory is equipped with high-end hardware and specialized software to facilitate research and practical learning in digital image analysis, remote sensing, GIS, computer vision, and forensic computing. The lab houses 16 HP computer systems powered by Intel Core i7-13700 processors, 16 GB RAM, 1 TB HDD, and 256 GB NVMe SSDs, all running Windows 11 Pro with integrated Intel UHD graphics, offering a robust platform for high-resolution image processing and data-intensive tasks. A 28-port D-Link managed network switch ensures seamless data transfer and connectivity, while the VERTIV Powerbank 600 UPS with 16 Exide SMF batteries (12V, 120 AH) provides reliable power backup. The lab also includes an HP LaserJet M1005 MFP printer for documentation and an interactive smart board to enhance teaching and demonstrations.
The lab is further enhanced with advanced software tools such as ERDAS Imagine Professional (5-user OEM licenses), IMAGINE Expansion Pack, and GeoMedia Professional for satellite image processing, geospatial analysis, and mapping applications. For forensic and cybersecurity applications, the lab includes Belkasoft Evidence Center X for digital evidence analysis, Passware Xit Forensic for password recovery and file decryption, and a vulnerability scanner tool for system security testing. Although currently inactive, EIGAP software (licensed for 50 users) is also part of the lab’s software inventory. This comprehensive setup makes the lab a vital center for academic exploration, industry-oriented training, and interdisciplinary research in image processing, GIS, computer vision, and digital forensics.
Programming Laboratory
The Programming Laboratory is designed to support foundational and advanced programming courses, catering to First Year (FY), Second Year (SY), and Third Year (TY) students. Spread across 91.94 sq. m. with a seating capacity for 20 students, the lab is equipped with 20 Dell computer systems powered by Intel Core i7-8700 CPUs @ 3.20GHz, 4 GB RAM, 1 TB HDD, and 256 GB NVMe SSDs, running Windows 11 Home. These systems provide a capable environment for learning and practicing programming across various languages and platforms. The lab has essential software tools installed, including MS Office 2013, C, C++, Java, Python, Jupyter, and Visual Studio, ensuring a comprehensive development and debugging environment. Additionally, a CodeZinger subscription for 475 users enhances coding practice through auto-evaluated programming challenges. The lab supports a utilization of 870 student-hours per semester across all academic wings, reflecting its critical role in curriculum delivery. The Programming Lab stands as a core facility for nurturing programming skills and software development competencies.
Advanced Software Engineering Lab
The Advanced Software Engineering Laboratory is a high-capacity, well-equipped facility designed to support project-based learning and development in software engineering and enterprise applications. Spanning an area of 81.94 sq. m. with a seating capacity for 50 students, the lab is equipped with 50 Dell computer systems powered by Intel Core i7-8700 CPUs @ 3.20GHz, 4 GB RAM, 1 TB HDD, and 256 GB NVMe SSDs, all running on Windows 11 Home. The lab supports comprehensive software development environments with essential tools such as MS Office 2013, Oracle, SQL Developer, GitHub, Jira, and Microsoft 365 A3 subscription, enabling students to engage in end-to-end software project lifecycle activities. Visual and instructional support is provided via an Epson EB-945H LCD projector, while lab security is maintained with CCTV surveillance. A robust network infrastructure is established through six high-performance switches including models from TRENDnet, Netgear, and Extreme Networks. Continuous power backup is ensured by a 20 KVA Emerson GXT MT Online UPS supported by 20 Turbon SMF batteries (12V, 180 AH). Additionally, an Ahuja SSB-80M amplifier supports communication needs during sessions. The lab supports FY, SY, and TY students, with a utilization rate of 600 student-hours per semester. This lab plays a pivotal role in delivering advanced software engineering education through practical and collaborative learning.
Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Laboratory
The Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Laboratory is a dedicated facility designed to support AI/ML-centric education, research, and development activities. The lab features a heterogeneous set of 22 computer systems from HP and Dell, equipped with a range of processors including Intel Core i5-6550, i5-3470, i7-4700, i7-2600, and powerful Intel Xeon E3-1220 CPUs. These systems are configured with RAM capacities ranging from 4 GB to 16 GB and 1 TB HDD storage, offering a flexible environment suitable for running AI algorithms, machine learning models, and data processing tasks. The lab also includes a ViewSonic LCD projector (Model RLC 129) to facilitate interactive teaching and presentations. For effective communication during lab sessions or workshops, a 240W amplifier with mixer, Bluetooth, and USB support is available. This setup provides students with essential computational resources and instructional tools for exploring real-world AI and machine learning applications, ranging from predictive analytics to neural networks and data visualization.
Innovation and Project Laboratory
The Innovation and Project Laboratory is a cutting-edge facility designed to nurture creativity, research, and interdisciplinary project development in fields such as robotics, drones, embedded systems, AI, and aeromodelling. The lab provides a rich ecosystem of prototyping tools and devices to support student innovations. Core resources include 3 standards and 3 carbon fiber hexacopter drone frames, 6 Pixhawk flight controllers, 6 FS-i6X (and above) RC controllers, 30 ESC 30A units, 30 propellers (10×5), 30 brushless motors, and 2 high-speed 2200KV motors. Power requirements are addressed with 6 LiPo batteries (2500 mAh), 6 LiPo batteries (1000 mAh), and a fast battery charger. Additionally, a DJI Tello drone with an extra battery, a telemetry kit, landing gear, and soldering tools are available to streamline the development and testing process.
For robotic and autonomous systems, the lab features a Dobot Magician Robotic Arm, Turtle Bot, and Jetson Nano Developer Kit, enabling students to build and test intelligent automation solutions. Advanced perception and navigation capabilities are supported by Intel RealSense Depth Cameras (3 units), YD Lidar G2, RP Lidar A3, and a RTK Module (Receiver and Transmitter) for high-accuracy positioning. Moreover, a Snapmaker 3-in-1 CNC machine is available for multifunctional prototyping, combining 3D printing, laser engraving, and CNC carving. The lab also supports aeromodelling with 2 RC plane frames and 24 servo motors.
This extensive infrastructure encourages experiential learning and supports capstone projects, robotics competitions, and applied research across multiple domains, making the Innovation and Project Lab a hub of technological exploration and invention.
PG Research Laboratory
The Postgraduate (PG) Research Laboratory is a high-performance computing and research facility established to support advanced postgraduate studies, simulations, and innovation-driven research across domains such as data science, AI, cybersecurity, and high-end graphics computing. The lab houses 10 powerful HP computer systems, each equipped with Intel Core i7-13700 processors @ 2.10GHz, 16 GB RAM, 1 TB HDD, 500 GB NVMe SSD, and NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 graphics, providing the required computing power for deep learning, visualization, and parallel processing tasks. These systems run on Windows 11 Pro, offering a modern and secure operating environment.
For seamless networking and high-speed data transfer, the lab is supported by enterprise-grade switches including the Extreme X440 G2 24t-10GE4 and Extreme 5320-24T-8XE, ensuring reliable and scalable connectivity. An Epson EB-X14 LCD projector enhances presentations and research discussions, while an Epson L565 All-in-One printer supports documentation and report generation needs. Power continuity is ensured by a 6KVA Vertiv UPS supported by 16 SMF batteries, minimizing interruptions during critical research work. This advanced infrastructure makes the PG Research Lab a dynamic hub for scholarly research, technical innovation, and collaborative academic exploration at the postgraduate level.
PG Computing Laboratory
The Postgraduate (PG) Computing Laboratory is a dedicated facility aimed at supporting advanced coursework, research, and development activities in computing-intensive domains. The lab is equipped with a total of 10 HP computer systems featuring the latest Intel Core i7-13700 processors @ 2.10GHz, 16 GB RAM, 1 TB HDD, and 500 GB NVMe SSDs, ensuring high-speed performance and responsiveness. Of these, 6 systems are equipped with **NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060** graphics cards, ideal for tasks involving deep learning, data visualization, simulations, and parallel computing, while the remaining 4 systems come with **Intel UHD Graphics**, suitable for general-purpose computing and programming. All systems operate on **Windows 11 Pro**, providing a secure and modern computing environment. With its high-performance infrastructure, the PG Computing Lab facilitates academic research, project implementation, and exploration of advanced computing technologies for postgraduate students and scholars.
The department has various centres, such as the Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, and the Centre for Cybersecurity.
Cyber security server:
Cybersecurity is vital for computer science engineering as it ensures the protection of data, systems, and networks from malicious attacks.
With increasing digitalization, safeguarding sensitive information and maintaining system integrity are critical. This server is set up with the aim of developing a center of excellence (CoE) in Cyber Security.
The server offers functionality such as: password recovery, hard disk recovery, vulnerability scanning

To have at least 4-5 startups from the teams participating for the Onsite Hackathon.
At least 3-5 patent filing from the teams participating Onsite Hackathon.
To get a transition from University to Industrial Hackathon.

Some students will be provided an in house research internship in summer or winter vacation period.
Mentor-Mentee Program
Department has prepared a Mentor-Mentee program. Each mentor has 20 students in their group. Monthly mentor-mentee meetings are conducted for review of one month’s progress and resolution of any problems faced by students.

B Tech Curriculum with Minors
B.Tech Curriculum with Minors
Curriculum
– The B.Tech curriculum in Information Technology is designed to provide students with a comprehensive education in Information Technology.
In the Academic Year 2024-2025 curriculum of First year and Second Year is implemented as per NEP 2020 policy which includes multidisciplinary minor (MDM) as well. IT department offers MDM in Information Technology and FinTech (14 credits).
Minors –
The department offers minors in areas such as Operating System, Computer Network, Software Engineering and Data Visualization and Analysis
Program Objective and Outcome
Graduates of UG Programme after completing their graduation in Information Technology will be able to:
PEO1:
Demonstrate technical competency by applying knowledge to solve problems related to Engineering issues.
PEO2:
Exhibit high professional skills and ethical attitude to succeed in their professional career.
PEO3:
Display thirst for emerging technologies and quest for research and innovation to solve real-world problems of high complexity, with concern to society and environment
Program Outcomes
PO1:
Engineering Knowledge: Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems.
PO2: Problem Analysis:
Identify, formulate, review research literature, and Analyse complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences.
PO3: Design/Development of Solutions: D
esign solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for the public health and safety, and the cultural, societal, and environmental considerations.
PO4: Conduct Investigations of Complex Problems:
Use research-based knowledge and research methods including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of the information to provide valid conclusions.
PO5: Modern Tool Usage:
Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools including prediction and modelling to complex engineering activities with an understanding of the limitations.
PO6: The Engineer and Society:
Apply reasoning informed by the contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to the professional engineering practice
PO7: Environment and Sustainability:
Understand the impact of the professional engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts, and demonstrate the knowledge of, and need for sustainable development.
PO8: Ethics:
Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities and norms of the engineering practice.
PO9: Individual and Team Work:
Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams, and in multidisciplinary settings.
PO10: Communication:
Communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the engineering community and with society at large, such as, being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations, and give and receive clear instructions.
PO11: Project Management and Finance:
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the engineering and management principles and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team, to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.
PO12:
Life-long learning: Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change.
Program Specific Outcomes
PSO1:
Apply Software Engineering practices, Programming logic, networking techniques and Information Storage Management in project development process.
PSO2
: Conceptualize ideas into IT based solutions with industry interaction using cutting edge technologies such as Data Mining, High Performance Computing, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Computer Vision and Information Security
Outcome Based Educational Philosophy
Outcome Based Education (OBE) is top down approach to comply with Vision, Mission, PEOs, POs and COs for development of academics and students. However, the bottom up approach is also followed to attain COs, POs, PEOs and VMO of department and institute through teaching learning process. The direct attainment from continuous assessment and indirect attainment from students, graduates, employers, alumni and parents feedbacks helps to achieve targeted attainment in OBE.

M. Tech Specialisations and Curriculum
M.Tech Specialisations and Curriculum
Specialisations:
The M.Tech in Data Science at Walchand College of Engineering (WCE), offered by the IT Department, provides a strong foundation in advanced knowledge of data science field, modern data technologies, and research methodologies. It focuses on areas like artificial Intelligence, machine learning, data analysis/analytics, Data visualization and mathematics. It provides various tracks for specialization using Professional elective Bucket list. The program prepares students for roles in research, academia, and industry.
Curriculum –
The M.Tech curriculum is designed to provide students with advanced knowledge and skills in their chosen specialisation. The curriculum is designed to provide students with a comprehensive education in Data science and engineering. M.Tech (Data Science) curriculum is started in 2024-2025 and it is designed as per  NEP 2020 policy.
Program Educational Objectives (PEOs)
Post graduates on successful completion of the programme in Data Science will be able to:
PEO 1
:  Contribute individually and in a team to carry out data collection and processing for the development of Data Science methodologies with professional skills.
PEO 2:
Apply domain expertise to interpret data and demonstrate technical competency in handling real life projects by analysing, evaluating and synthesizing the information.
PEO 3:
Exhibit continuous learning attitude, ethical behaviour and techno-socio responsibilities as an expert in Data Science field.
Program Outcomes (POs)
On successful completion of the programme of post-graduation in Data Science, students will be able to:
PO1:
Apply appropriate data handling skills and techniques for development of practical solutions in the domain of Data Science
(Research Skill)
PO2:
Demonstrate comprehensive understanding of Data Science theories, knowledge, principles, methodologies, and tools to address complex data challenges
(Scholarship of Knowledge)
PO3
: Conceptualize and solve data engineering problems to find feasible and optimal solutions
(Critical Thinking and problem solving)
PO4:
Communicate research work to the scientific and societal community through technical reports, publications and IPR’s
(Communication)
PO5:
Exhibit ethical and professional code of conduct for life-long learning and providing sustainable solution on societal issues
(Ethical Practices, Social responsibility, Managerial skills and Life-long learning)
PO6:
Recommend suitable mechanisms including data handling, processing, programming, visualising, transforming, interpreting, analysing, storing, managing and securing data for scalable data driven applications
(Program Specific Outcome)

Academic Planning & Activities
Academic Planning & Activities
The Information Technology Department implements several innovative and student-centric practices to ensure a well-rounded academic experience. These include:
Curriculum Design and Development
Integration of interdisciplinary courses (e.g., Data Mining, Web Technology, Artificial Intelligence, IoT).
Regular curriculum revisions to align with industry trends and accreditation guidelines (e.g.NBA, NAAC).
Inclusion of project-based and experiential learning modules.
Research and Innovation Initiatives
Establishing research groups for emerging fields like Robotics, Machine Learning, and Sustainable Engineering.
Collaboration with industry for funded research projects and internships.
Organizing hackathons, ideation contests, and innovation challenges.
Laboratory and Infrastructure Development
Upgrading labs with advanced machine like DELL OptiPlex 5000 and industry support lab as AR-VR lab .
Setting Research Lab for student.
Promoting virtual labs and remote experimentation for online learners.
Comprehensive Mentorship Program
Every class has a designated class teacher who monitors academic performance, attendance, and overall well-being.
Class Teachers collaborate with students to set academic and career goals while ensuring compliance with institutional requirements.
For A.Y.2024-2025 following class teachers assigned,
FY B.Tech –
Y.B.Tech – Dr Chavan U.B.
Y.B.Tech – Mrs.Shetty B.S.
Final Year B.Tech – Dr.Sonavane S.S.
Program Delivery with Emphasis on Experiential Learning
Integration of
project-based learning
across courses to develop problem-solving and analytical skills.
Collaboration with industry partners for live projects, case studies, and workshops on trending technologies.
Use of cutting-edge tools, simulation platforms, and online coding platforms to enhance the learning experience.
Projects and Mini-Projects
Students undertake
mini-projects
in fifth and sixth semesters and
major projects
in final year, encouraging application-based learning and research problem statements.
Projects often focus on solving real-world problems, with themes such as Smart Cities, E-Healthcare, and Green Computing.
Organizing project showcases and hackathons to promote innovation and teamwork.
Mini Project and mega project guides are assigned to each group to evaluate student progress.
Industry Visits and Internships
Regular
industrial visits
to top IT companies, start-ups, and research centres provide students with practical exposure to organizational workflows and cutting-edge technologies.
Internship opportunities during semester breaks enable students to gain hands-on experience in real-world projects and applications.
Students are exposed to work outside the campus to know the industry environment & working.
It gives knowledge to the students about the real life experiments, industry culture that improves self-confidence, team spirit.
Seminars, Workshops, and Technical Events
Regular
departmental seminars
and
guest lectures
by industry professionals and academic experts on emerging trends like Data Science, Machine Learning etc.
Workshops on programming languages, frameworks, and tools such as Python.
Hosting hackathons, coding contests and innovation challenges to foster creativity and competitive spirit among students.
Skill Development Initiatives
Conducting soft skills development workshops focusing on communication, teamwork, and leadership.
Research-Oriented Activities
Active student-run clubs such as Coding Club, Robotics Club, and Linux Club,ASCES club to promote peer learning.
Organizing intra- and inter-college competitions to encourage networking and knowledge sharing.
Our Students are growing through club culture in curricular and extra curricular activities.
Technical Clubs and Extracurricular Activities
Establishing research groups in fields like Machine Learning, IoT, and Cybersecurity.
Encouraging students to publish research papers, participate in technical conferences, and apply for innovation grants.
Collaboration with faculty to develop innovative solutions and products for industry and societal challenges.
Continuous Evaluation and Improvement
Regular feedback from students and faculty on teaching methods, curriculum design, and overall experience.
Adapting to the latest trends in technology and pedagogy to maintain academic excellence.
Continuous Evaluation is done for laboratory courses by taking Laboratory Assessment 1 and 2(30 Marks) End Semester Examination (40 Mark)
Continuous Evaluation for the theory courses are taken in the form of In semester evaluation 1 and 2 (20 Mark) Mid Semester Evaluation (30 Mark) End Semester Evaluation(50 Mark)
In semester evaluation taken in the form of Oral, Quiz, Presentation, MCQ etc.
Industry-Academia Collaboration
Partnerships for internships, co-op programs, and guest lectures.
Inviting industry experts for curriculum input and mentorship.
